frame, refines orientation through circular-to-local residual
distributions,andalignsclassificationandlocalizationusing
complete-OBB quality. Experiments on DOTA-1.0, DIOR-
R, and AI-TOD-R demonstrate consistent localization gains
with comparable computational cost, establishing a better
speed–accuracy trade-off for real-time oriented object de-
tection.Limitation and Future Work:We further observe
anincreasinglypronouncedtrade-offamongevaluationmet-
rics between recall and precision as detector performance
improves in the field of oriented object detection. Future
work may focus on balancing overall detection quality and
developing more informative evaluation protocols. We also
encourage future studies to report

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance gains over RiO-DETR and existing detectors align with empirical tables, particularly demonstrating higher accuracy on strict localization thresholds (mAP50-95 and AP75) with negligible computational overhead.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The model is evaluated across three established aerial detection benchmarks (DOTA-1.0 official test server, DIOR-R, and AI-TOD-R) across five model scales, reporting standardized mAP50-95, AP50, AP75, and TensorRT latency measurements against relevant real-time baselines. Component ablations and in-depth analyses of distributional uncertainty and near-square degeneracies validate specific design claims.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly analyze precision-recall trade-offs across varying thresholds, the impact of confidence calibration on AP50, and representation ambiguities (canonical-axis exchange) for near-square objects.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, formulating boundary distributions in an object-aligned coordinate frame, handling rotational periodicity through circular-to-local residual refinement, and supervising multi-task branches using Gaussian KLD-derived complete-OBB localization quality alongside distribution-aware confidence calibration.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a sound, well-motivated architectural extension to real-time oriented DETRs with thorough mathematical descriptions, clear ablation studies, and robust benchmarking on standard datasets without methodological circularity.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RiO-DETRv2, an end-to-end real-time oriented object detection transformer incorporating Object-Aligned Boundary Distribution Refinement, Circular-to-Local Angular Residual Refinement, and Unified OBB Quality-Aligned Learning.

Gaussian
representation learning with hierarchical 3D scene graph con-
struction. PanoGraphGS jointly learns semantic and instance
features anchored to shared Gaussian geometry. The semantic
branch combines residual feature projection and category
prototypes with confidence-weighted supervision, while the
instance branch associates view-local pseudo-labels with
persistent Gaussian instance identities to ensure consistent
object correspondence across views. As illustrated in Fig. 1,
the resulting panoptic Gaussian representation supports both
panoptic segmentation and direct Gaussian-level decoding.
The semantic-aware hierarchical reasoning module combines
structural semantics with Gaussian geometry to recover the
floor-room-stuff-objecthierarchy and its containment and
spatial relations, enabling structured spatial queries such as
locating the bed1 in the living room on floor1. CLIP

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript reports evaluation against external benchmark ground-truth annotations on ScanNet++, Replica, and NaviGS for panoptic segmentation metrics, and manually verified hierarchical ground truth for scene graph accuracy.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External benchmark ground-truth annotations for 2D panoptic segmentation (mIoU, mBIoU) and manually verified hierarchical ground truth for 3D scene graph accuracy.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: SAM3-generated 2D pseudo-segmentation masks combined with photometric RGB losses and confidence-weighted contrastive/prototype losses.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported empirical improvements in hierarchical accuracy and panoptic boundary quality align with the proposed joint 2D-3D representations and association mechanisms [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0021, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0027, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0036].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is evaluated against established baselines (HOV-SG, ConceptGraphs, Unified-Lift, PanopticRecon++) across three datasets (ScanNet++, Replica, NaviGS) on 2D panoptic segmentation (mIoU, mBIoU) and 3D scene graph identification accuracy, supported by an ablation study [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0021, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0027, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0036].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard external ground-truth masks and annotations on ScanNet++, Replica, and NaviGS are used to compute mIoU/mBIoU and scene graph accuracy [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0030, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0031].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard ground-truth benchmark annotations for 2D panoptic segmentation (mIoU, mBIoU) and manually verified hierarchical ground truth for 3D scene graph accuracy [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0030, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0031].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: SAM3-generated 2D pseudo-segmentation masks combined with photometric RGB losses and confidence-weighted contrastive/prototype losses [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0013, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0019, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0022].

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge limitations, including poor room boundary delineation in open-plan spaces (e.g., open kitchens) and the offline nature of the scene graph construction [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0040].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the shared rendering formulations, residual projection MLP for prototype semantics, Hungarian matching for view-consistent global instance assignment, confidence weighting, and hierarchical rule-based graph construction from structural Gaussians [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0015, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0016, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0018, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0020, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0025, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0027].
primary.quality_rationale: The paper presents a coherent technical framework, solid algorithmic details, clear baselines, rigorous ablation analysis, and appropriate limitations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript proposes PanoGraphGS, an approach combining 3D Gaussian Splatting with prototype-based semantic learning and Hungarian association-based instance learning, together with a semantic-aware floor-room-stuff-object scene graph construction pipeline and a new benchmark dataset NaviGS [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0002, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0008, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0018, Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0025].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper presents a coherent technical framework, solid algorithmic details, clear baselines, rigorous ablation analysis, and appropriate limitations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge limitations, including poor room boundary delineation in open-plan spaces (e.g., open kitchens) and the offline nature of the scene graph construction [Eb2ed8061a1ca8742-B0040].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Astrometry.net solving success and Gaia DR3 positional residuals provide an external, objective measurement of the recovered WCS solutions, independent of the detector's training labels.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcome is astrometric recovery of previously failed plates via Astrometry.net blind solving and positional residuals against epoch-propagated Gaia DR3 coordinates, plus throughput measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training and fine-tuning use bounding-box and class labels generated by SExtractor detections cross-matched with Gaia DR3, including the Gaia-guided target-domain labels built from initially solved UBAI plates.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims closely match the empirical evidence, showing that Plate-YOLO accelerates source extraction compared to SExtractor, achieves high calibration recovery on severely degraded plates, and yields comparable or slightly improved astrometric RMS residuals.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation combines component ablations on the source archive, cross-archive zero-shot and fine-tuned astrometric recovery on 150 previously failed UBAI plates (achieving 146/150 recovered), detection completeness and purity analyses, and astrometric residual comparisons relative to external Gaia DR3 coordinates across 500 plates.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final plate calibration success via Astrometry.net and independent positional residual calculations (RMS relative to epoch-propagated Gaia DR3 coordinates) corroborate the object detection performance.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Astrometric blind solving success and WCS coordinate registration residuals against external Gaia DR3 catalog coordinates, along with processing throughput measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training using ground-truth bounding box regression and classification labels generated by SExtractor detections cross-matched with Gaia DR3 catalogs on historical plate collections.

primary.limitations: The authors document residual dependency on reference catalog depth, sensitivity degradation for the faintest sources, failure on extended comet plates with trailed stars, and caution that instrumental magnitude rank correlations do not constitute calibrated photometry.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is comprehensively described, integrating architecture adjustments into YOLOv5 for micro-scale point sources, an objective Gaia-cross-matched pseudo-labeling strategy, and an instrumental brightness proxy for ranking detections before passing them to Astrometry.net.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a well-executed domain adaptation and detection pipeline that solves a concrete problem in historical astronomical archive preservation, backed by sound ablation studies and solid independent validation via Gaia DR3 astrometric calibration.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Plate-YOLO, an end-to-end object detector combining source detection and stellar classification tailored for degraded historical astronomical photographic plates using Space-to-Depth modules, SimAM attention, a micro-scale P2 head, Normalized Wasserstein Distance loss, and a cross-archive fine-tuning strategy.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a well-executed domain adaptation and detection pipeline that solves a concrete problem in historical astronomical archive preservation, backed by sound ablation studies and solid independent validation via Gaia DR3 astrometric calibration.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors document residual dependency on reference catalog depth, sensitivity degradation for the faintest sources, failure on extended comet plates with trailed stars, and caution that instrumental magnitude rank correlations do not constitute calibrated photometry.

1) Methods for comparison:As most EBSPE methods are
per-event-frame-based (Sec. II-A), we compare against the
current SOTA method from [4], referred to here as "Event-
frame" (EF). EF processes each event frame independently
through OD, followed by cropping and HR. The methods
that employed fixed-time windows [13], [14] were not di-
rectly compared due to the lack of publicly available code
implementation. Instead, we assess the effect of fixed-time
windows through an ablation study (Sec. V-F).
2) Benchmark datasets:Both RVT-P and EF were trained
and evaluated on E-PROSPER data spanning all speeds,
lighting conditions, and targets, with no sequence overlap
between the training and test sets. Additionally,traj6and
traj12were reserved entirely for testing. The resulting
train/validation/test split was 33/17/50. We also separately
trained and evaluated both methods on FRESH [4]

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline pose gains are measured against external ground-truth transforms from calibrated UR5 trajectories and checkerboard targets, independent of the training losses.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pose accuracy is reported via geometric translation and rotation errors against robotic manipulator ground-truth trajectories, resolved through EPnP/RANSAC.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training uses object detection losses (IoU, classification, regression) and landmark heatmap regression loss against ground-truth annotations.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding superior pose accuracy and stability under slow relative motion are supported by the empirical metrics on E-PROSPER, while the authors transparently report failure modes on out-of-distribution dynamics (FRESH) and unseen trajectories.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is conducted using robotic ground truth on the E-PROSPER dataset across multiple speeds (0.001 to 0.05 m/s) and lighting conditions, comparing against the state-of-the-art frame-based baseline and a fixed-window ablation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Pose errors are measured objectively against external ground-truth transforms obtained from calibrated UR5 robotic manipulator trajectories and checkerboard targets.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard geometric 6DoF translation and rotation errors evaluated against independent robotic manipulator ground-truth trajectories via EPnP.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training using object detection loss (IoU/classification/regression) and landmark heatmap regression loss against ground-truth annotations.

primary.limitations: The authors document the degraded performance when tested on unseen trajectory viewpoints and out-of-distribution synthetic-to-real transfer on FRESH, noting dependencies on training temporal diversity.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing voxel grid tensor representations, recurrent spatial-temporal transformer blocks with LSTM states, an adapted landmark heatmap regressor, and EPnP/RANSAC pose resolution.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-scoped contribution addressing the known failure mode of event sensors under slow relative motion in space operations. The experimental setup provides rigorous robotic ground truth, fair comparative evaluations, and transparent analysis of limitations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces RVT-P, an architecture adapting recurrent vision transformers with heatmap regression and PnP for event-based 6DoF spacecraft pose estimation under slow relative motions, accompanied by the E-PROSPER real-event evaluation dataset collected using a robotic manipulator and space-grade sensor.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-scoped contribution addressing the known failure mode of event sensors under slow relative motion in space operations. The experimental setup provides rigorous robotic ground truth, fair comparative evaluations, and transparent analysis of limitations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors document the degraded performance when tested on unseen trajectory viewpoints and out-of-distribution synthetic-to-real transfer on FRESH, noting dependencies on training temporal diversity.

Once historical clients become unavailable, a federation
must serve newcomers through the artifact it leaves behind.
How much of its knowledge remains useful in an architec-
ture chosen afterward? We introduceFEDNBO, a seven-
dataset benchmark that separates knowledge supply, policy
identification, and private-model compilation under disjoint
data roles. Controlled studies expose inflated oracle gains,
architecture-dependent transfer reversals, and a gap be-
tween teacher accuracy and private-model utility. Ordinary
public-response distillation provides a competitive reference
without public task labels or newcomer samples: gains over
strengthened local training are 23.52 and 16.62 percent-
age points on 300 CelebA identities and 300 FedEMNIST
writers, respectively. In a complete-pipeline FedEMNIST
comparison, this reference reaches 97.13% accuracy with
12.4 seconds of compilation per

Once historical clients become unavailable, a federation
must serve newcomers through the artifact it leaves behind.
How much of its knowledge remains useful in an architec-
ture chosen afterward? We introduceFEDNBO, a seven-
dataset benchmark that separates knowledge supply, policy
identification, and private-model compilation under disjoint
data roles. Controlled studies expose inflated oracle gains,
architecture-dependent transfer reversals, and a gap be-
tween teacher accuracy and private-model utility. Ordinary
public-response distillation provides a competitive reference
without public task labels or newcomer samples: gains over
strengthened local training are 23.52 and 16.62 percent-

comparison, this reference reaches 97.13% accuracy with

evidence.excerpt:
Source clients train the bank; shadow (meta) clients select
policies before held-out test scoring (Table 1). Prospective
studies freeze plans before test access. Labeled revisions
reuse evaluated cohorts but make new choices on shadow-
development clients. The five-dataset policy audit repeats
optimization with five seeds and linear/deep heads; UCI
HAR uses linear models and temporal CNNs. Seeds are not
independent clients. MELD assigns modalities by speaker
and preserves dialogue separation. UCF51-20 preserves in-
divisible video groups; its clients are simulated. TCGA uses
eligible Tissue Source Sites and class-stratified 60/20/20
splits. UCI HAR withholds gyroscope from half the sub-
jects; FedEMNIST preserves writer identities and official
within-writer partitions. Cohort and freeze receipts are sup-
plementary.

evidence.excerpt:
NIST uses 4,096 images from 500 public writers to compile
unseen pixel-MLP/CNN models. Neither compiler uses pub-
lic task labels or newcomer inputs; the primary decentralized
revision removes the historical public-label progression gate.
Selectors include fixed policies, empirical selection-label
argmax,Active Testing(fixed ensemble surrogate, expected-
loss acquisition, 10% uniform floor and LURE correc-
tion [11]),PCV(one shadow-selected policy, requiring non-
negative mean gain for every shadow client), and Eq. 4.
Local wins ties; same-query oracles are diagnostic. HAR
additionally executes PeFLL-compatible generation from 12
labeled descriptors and ATP-compatible one-step entropy
adaptation from 20 unlabeled inputs [3, 20]; their supported
interfaces and references differ.

HAR freezes roles, missingness, five policies and budgets
before opening 12 test subjects; a shadow-only amendment
sets two fit labels per class. Fixed KD-1 gains 3.88 pp over-
all but loses 1.73 pp in linear models and gains 9.49 pp in
temporal CNNs (Fig. 3D). The paired interaction is11.21 pp
[7.57,15.17], p=.0005 by exact sign-flip. Six disagreement
labels halve harm from 16.7% to 8.3%; 24 retain that harm
and raise gain to 4.47 pp (Table 4A). Neither removes neg-
ative linear-stratum gain. Architecture routing discovered
here remains retrospective.

evidence.excerpt:
This supplement follows the four experimental questions in the main paper: selection, private-model realization, public-input
support, and cost/benefit. The main paper presents the principal policy, architecture, support, and budget contrasts. The
consolidated tables here retain their original context and additional shadow, historical-control, and source-search rows. Full
grids and individual seeds remain in the accompanying JSON/CSV files.
Roles and uncertainty.Source clients train the bank; shadow-development clients choose recipes; shadow-validation and
test clients evaluate frozen decisions. Revisions explicitly reuse previously evaluated cohorts. The primary revised CelebA and

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline performance is evaluated using true ground-truth labels from held-out test splits across natural clients and writers, accompanied by client-bootstrap confidence intervals.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Task-specific target evaluation metrics (classification accuracy and balanced accuracy) scored on held-out newcomer test query sets whose labels are strictly withheld during compilation.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Response distillation loss (KL/BCE matching frozen bank teacher logits on unlabeled public anchor inputs) and local fit labels.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings closely reflect empirical results: the authors explicitly demonstrate where distillation succeeds (e.g., substantial gains on CelebA and FedEMNIST) and openly highlight where transfer fails, produces negative transfer, or causes client harm (e.g., CREMA-D and linear HAR models).
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation is remarkably comprehensive, testing simple public-response KD against strengthened local controls, hypernetwork generators, and test-time personalization baselines across multiple modalities. It thoroughly audits failure modes, reporting client harm rates, anchor support interventions, cost amortizations, and the hazards of same-query selection optimism.

primary.limitations: The manuscript transparently discusses key constraints, including small test cohorts for MELD/TCGA, simulated action silos, in-domain public anchors, lack of formal differential privacy guarantees, and the non-equivalence of finite sample guarantees to prospective individual safety.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is exceptionally rigorous, strictly formalizing role-disjoint protocols (source, public anchors, shadow clients, and evaluation-only test query sets) and mathematically proving identifiability limits and mean-gain concentration certificates. Model compilation and baseline methods are carefully specified across distinct architecture types without target query label leakage.
primary.quality_rationale: This work sets a high standard for benchmarking post-federation transfer by combining theoretical grounding with scrupulously controlled experiments, pre-registered chronologies, and explicit disclosures of both positive and negative outcomes. It clearly qualifies for acceptance.
primary.scoped_contribution: FEDNBO introduces a seven-dataset benchmark and formal decomposition (supply, identification, compilation) to evaluate post-federation knowledge transfer into unseen, newcomer-chosen private architectures using disjoint data roles and declared onboarding evidence.

Given our prior analysis of where the hardest samples lie and whether fidelity or coverage can predict
it, we experiment with two formulations: a fidelity-based one that matches the data distribution via
the sliced Wasserstein distance, and a coverage-based one that spreads the coreset over the data via
farthest-point sampling (FPS). Each axis of z(x) is first standardized to unit variance over the dataset
so that no axis dominates the distance. We apply a redundancy heuristic such that an axis is removed
when its correlation with another exceeds 0.95, which holds for σ12 and µ12 on Cityscapes (all
variants), NA VSIM, SemanticKITTI-DVPS, and often on LIBERO-10, ensuring that the remaining
axes are decorrelated and each contributes independent information to selection. For fidelity, we

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline gains are established by ground-truth-labeled downstream benchmarks and simulator-based policy evaluations, which do not depend on the foundation model used for feature extraction or on the coverage/fidelity scores used to choose selection axes.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Downstream task metrics (classification accuracy, mIoU, RMSE, EPDMS, LIBERO success rate) computed from independently trained task models on held-out evaluation splits.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The selection axes (mu12, sigma12, delta_max) are chosen by correlating coreset-level coverage and fidelity scores against downstream performance across 5,265 historical training runs, and the selection procedure itself is tuned via ablations on CIFAR10 downstream accuracy.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance metrics directly align with the claims: CoreDNA matches or outperforms baselines across diverse perception and action benchmarks, demonstrating robustness to redundancy and practical utility without task-specific tuning or labels.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation spans multiple tasks (image classification, semantic segmentation, metric depth estimation, and imitation learning for driving and manipulation) across seven benchmarks and compares CoreDNA against nine training-based and training-free baselines across multiple retention ratios with three seeds.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final model performance is measured via ground-truth task labels and benchmark metrics on held-out evaluation splits completely independent of the feature extraction model.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective downstream task test metrics (classification accuracy, mIoU, RMSE, NAVSIM EPDMS, and LIBERO success rate) from independently trained task models.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Foundation model neuron activation histogram statistics pooled relative to the full dataset distribution.

primary.limitations: The authors openly address that optimal sampling strategies (fidelity vs. coverage) vary depending on dataset tail characteristics, and note that fixed retention ratios or redundant modalities (e.g., manipulation proprioception) do not uniformly improve performance.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing per-neuron Earth Mover's Distance extraction relative to the dataset, layerwise statistic pooling into a compact representation space, and concrete selection algorithms (sliced Wasserstein minimization and FPS) with explicit pseudo-code and parameter settings.
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides a well-motivated, scalable solution to label-free coreset selection backed by rigorous empirical analysis of activation distributions across 5,265 historical runs, clear algorithmic formulations, and comprehensive downstream cross-domain evaluations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces CoreDNA, an unsupervised and task-agnostic coreset selection method that summarizes multi-layer foundation model activation histograms relative to full-dataset distributions, selecting data subsets using sliced Wasserstein distance or farthest-point sampling.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides a well-motivated, scalable solution to label-free coreset selection backed by rigorous empirical analysis of activation distributions across 5,265 historical runs, clear algorithmic formulations, and comprehensive downstream cross-domain evaluations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors openly address that optimal sampling strategies (fidelity vs. coverage) vary depending on dataset tail characteristics, and note that fixed retention ratios or redundant modalities (e.g., manipulation proprioception) do not uniformly improve performance.

Models and calibration.All experiments run on
NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 80 GB of memory. The CIFAR
models and both SDT models use LIF neurons, and
SEW-ResNet-18 uses IF neurons. Weight calibration uses
a single seed, and on CIFAR-10 at W2, SpikeQ averages
90.52±0.19over three calibration seeds. All COCO
results, including full precision, are evaluated in FP32 with
TF32 disabled.
Weight quantization.Weights are quantized per output
channel. GPTQ and SBC use their default min-max grids,
and GPTAQ usesα= 0.25, the default of its official im-
plementation. BRECQ, PTQ4SNN, and SpikeQ share the
same clipping search for the weight grid, which minimizes
theL 2.4 weight error, so they differ only in the selected lev-
els. BRECQ and PTQ4SNN use 20k reconstruction itera-
tions (5k on COCO). On COCO, all methods keep the first
layer and the detection head at 8 bits with round-to-nearest.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final results are reported as top-1 accuracy, mIoU, and AP/AP50 on held-out benchmark evaluation sets, which do not use the spike-matching calibration objectives.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard ground-truth task metrics (top-1 accuracy, mIoU, AP/AP50) on benchmark validation/test sets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The spike-count, margin, and population losses computed against full-precision and local spike references during calibration.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that spike preservation drives downstream task fidelity and that threshold anchoring prevents low-bit pre-fire collapse are directly corroborated by empirical results (e.g., maintaining competitive mIoU and accuracy at 2-bit where conventional methods collapse).
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is rigorous and extensive, benchmarking pre-fire and post-reset quantization across seven distinct vision datasets and tasks (classification, segmentation, detection) and multiple SNN architectures, complete with ablations on each loss/grid component, energy modeling, and comparison against seven PTQ baselines.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final model evaluation relies on standard ground-truth benchmark metrics across ImageNet, CIFAR, VOC 2012, ADE20K, and COCO validation sets, entirely separate from the local spike-matching calibration objective.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard ground-truth task metrics (top-1 classification accuracy, mIoU, AP/AP50) evaluated on full held-out test/validation datasets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Spike-count loss, margin loss, and population loss computed on a small unlabeled calibration set (1,024 images for weights, 256 for membrane grids).

primary.limitations: The authors observe performance degradation when jointly compressing to 2-bit on complex tasks due to accumulating flipped spikes, and note that pre-fire quantization under soft reset requires a wider grid spanning above the threshold.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, specifying a discrete coordinate-search optimization for weights with spike count, margin, and population terms alongside a mathematically proven threshold-anchoring grid design that ensures pre-fire rounding avoids flipping spikes and aligns post-reset states to exact grid levels.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents sound theoretical and empirical justifications for departing from standard MSE-based PTQ objectives in spiking networks, executes a comprehensive set of controlled experiments, and clearly details all implementation aspects.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces SpikeQ, a spike-guided post-training quantization framework for spiking neural networks that quantizes weights by minimizing downstream spike errors and quantizes pre-fire membrane potentials using threshold-anchored, reset-aware grids.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents sound theoretical and empirical justifications for departing from standard MSE-based PTQ objectives in spiking networks, executes a comprehensive set of controlled experiments, and clearly details all implementation aspects.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors observe performance degradation when jointly compressing to 2-bit on complex tasks due to accumulating flipped spikes, and note that pre-fire quantization under soft reset requires a wider grid spanning above the threshold.

evidence.excerpt:
metrics 
All six configurations were evaluated on the same 
fixed set of 168 original validation observations 
obtained through source -separated partitioning. No 
sensor or random visual augmentation was applied 
during validation. Predictions were generated using 
the selected checkpoint for each configuration. 
Model performance was assessed using accuracy, 
macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1 -score, 
balanced accuracy, Cohen's kappa, and Matthews 
correlation coefficient (MCC). Macro averaging was 
used to assign equal importance to the four canonical 
classes. Balanced accuracy was calculated as the 
mean class -wise recall, while Cohen's kappa and 
MCC provided complementary measures of 
agreement and correlation beyond accuracy. 
In addition to record -level evaluation, source -
level performance was assessed by aggregating 
predicted class probabilities for observations

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline outcome is measured against ground-truth labels on a fixed source-separated validation split, and the shuffled-sensor control corroborates the null incremental effect of sensor correspondence.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Ground-truth class labels on a fixed, source-separated validation set of 168 observations, reported via accuracy, macro F1, balanced accuracy, MCC, and Cohen's kappa.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Multiclass cross-entropy loss against ground-truth disease labels, optimized with AdamW.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are strictly aligned with empirical observations; the paper clearly states that environmental data contains predictive signal in isolation (71.43% accuracy) but that multimodal integration does not demonstrate incremental accuracy gain over vision-only models.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation includes standard classification metrics across six configurations on a held-out source-separated validation set of 168 instances. The authors report that image-only baselines already saturate the benchmark at 100% accuracy, transparently confirming that multimodal fusion yields no incremental performance benefit under this test setup.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted using objective ground-truth category matching on a held-out source-separated validation split, supplemented by a shuffled-sensor negative control.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Classification accuracy, macro F1, balanced accuracy, MCC, and Cohen's kappa on a fixed, source-separated validation set using ground-truth class labels.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised cross-entropy loss against ground-truth disease class annotations optimized using AdamW.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly address limitations regarding dataset scope, ceiling effects on the validation partition, lack of cross-plantation and external environmental evaluation, and the need for more visually ambiguous field scenarios.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing network architectures, source-group-separated stratified partitioning to prevent data leakage, training-only data augmentations, and rigorous controls such as shuffled-sensor pairing.
primary.quality_rationale: The study demonstrates high methodological rigor, includes negative/neutral control outcomes (shuffled sensor and zero incremental gain over vision-only baselines), avoids overclaiming, provides reproducible artifacts, and accurately reports the boundaries of its contribution.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript presents a multimodal feature-fusion framework combining a Vision Transformer (ViT-Base) with an MLP encoding three agro-environmental sensor variables (humidity, soil moisture, pH) for coffee leaf disease classification, evaluated against unimodal baselines and a shuffled-sensor control on a source-partitioned dataset.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study demonstrates high methodological rigor, includes negative/neutral control outcomes (shuffled sensor and zero incremental gain over vision-only baselines), avoids overclaiming, provides reproducible artifacts, and accurately reports the boundaries of its contribution.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly address limitations regarding dataset scope, ceiling effects on the validation partition, lack of cross-plantation and external environmental evaluation, and the need for more visually ambiguous field scenarios.

title: Context-aware Multimodal Classification of Coffee Leaf Diseases Using Vision Transformer and Agro-environmental Sensor Data

The training objective is designed to supervise both frame-
level pose accuracy and temporal motion quality. Since the
output is a continuous root-relative skeleton sequence, only
minimizing the joint position error may still lead to frame-
wise fluctuations or locally distorted limb configurations.
Following standard practices in temporal 3D human pose
estimation [32]–[34], we combine a joint position loss with
first- and second-order temporal smoothness terms, and a
bone-length consistency constraint:
L=L pos +λ vLvel +λ aLacc +λ bLbone.(7)
Here,L pos penalizes joint position errors in the root-relative
skeleton space and provides the main supervision for pose
accuracy.L vel andL acc constrain first- and second-order
temporal differences, respectively, encouraging the predicted
motion to follow the reference dynamics and reducing high-
frequency jitter.L bone preserves local kinematic

evidence.excerpt:
All models are trained on 120-frame windows. The training
and validation windows are sampled with a step size of 5
frames, while testing uses a step size of 1 frame to obtain
dense frame-level predictions. The proposed fusion model uses
two-layer LSTM temporal modules with a hidden dimension
of 256. The upper- and lower-body branches use separate
temporal memories, and the global coordinator predicts resid-
ual updates for both branches. We train the model using
AdamW with cosine learning-rate scheduling and select the
best checkpoint according to validation PA-MPJPE. For fair
comparison, the vision-only temporal baseline and fusion
variants are trained under the same data split, window length,
and evaluation protocol.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Held-out Xsens MoCap reference labels, including MoCap-derived stance contact labels rather than insole pressure, corroborate the reported gains across action-disjoint and subject-disjoint splits.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, jitter, and gait metrics computed against held-out Xsens MoCap reference motion, with stance labels derived from MoCap trajectories rather than the insole input.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training against Xsens MoCap reference labels using joint position, temporal smoothness, and bone-length losses.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: The reported findings directly support the claims: insole fusion reliably maintains pose estimation during lower-body obstruction and complete dropouts, reduces MPJPE and temporal jitter, and improves gait-related contact estimation across unseen subjects and real occlusion obstacles.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The experimental validation is extensive and rigorous, covering three diverse visual backbones (MediaPipe, YOLOPose26, SAT-HMR), clean conditions, synthetic occlusion, real desk-induced occlusions, and visual dropouts. Ground truth is measured objectively with a commercial 17-sensor Xsens Awinda MoCap system across standard metrics (MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, jitter) and gait-specific biomechanical parameters (stance accuracy derived from MoCap, step distance, cadence), supplemented by cross-subject evaluations and mobile runtime benchmarks.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on separate reference motion capture (17-sensor Xsens Awinda) where stance ground truth is derived from MoCap trajectories rather than insole sensors, across action-disjoint and subject-disjoint held-out splits.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Objective geometric and dynamic metrics (MPJPE, PA-MPJPE, trajectory jerk jitter) and gait analysis parameters (heel-strike step distance, cadence, and MoCap-derived stance contact labels) compared against held-out Xsens MoCap recordings.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised optimization using AdamW on multi-task loss terms (root-relative joint position loss, temporal velocity/acceleration differences, and bone-length consistency) relative to synchronized Xsens MoCap reference labels.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge key limitations, including the reliance on root-relative skeletons rather than long-term absolute global trajectories due to lack of absolute global yaw reference, the need for wider demographic and activity testing, and remaining validation requirements in downstream clinical or ergonomic tasks.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed: visual backbones provide unified 2D/3D/SMPL keypoint representations split into upper- and lower-body branches, the lower branch fuses insole features via an MLP, separate LSTMs handle temporal dynamics, and a global coordinator shares cross-branch residual updates under position, velocity, acceleration, and bone-length loss constraints.
primary.quality_rationale: The study demonstrates high scientific quality with a clear, technically sound method, a well-synchronized novel dataset, solid comparisons against fair vision-only temporal baselines, thorough ablations, and objective ground-truth evaluation using optical/inertial MoCap reference tracking.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces a part-decoupled temporal fusion framework combining monocular visual pose estimators with smart insole sensing (four piezoresistive pressure points and 3-axis acceleration per foot) and provides a synchronized 890K-frame multimodal dataset to improve 3D human pose estimation during lower-body occlusions and visual dropouts.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study demonstrates high scientific quality with a clear, technically sound method, a well-synchronized novel dataset, solid comparisons against fair vision-only temporal baselines, thorough ablations, and objective ground-truth evaluation using optical/inertial MoCap reference tracking.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge key limitations, including the reliance on root-relative skeletons rather than long-term absolute global trajectories due to lack of absolute global yaw reference, the need for wider demographic and activity testing, and remaining validation requirements in downstream clinical or ergonomic tasks.

Learned memory control for SAM-based trackers.We formulate memory bank control in SAM-
based trackers as an MDP over a fixed-capacity bank. The state describes the content of the bank, the
action selects the entry to evict, and the reward scores the resulting prediction against the annotation.
This formulation allows the memory control to be learned instead of being manually designed.

ory controller obtained by optimizing the introduced MDP with RL. It improves over SAM 3 on 11

challenges, with+3.6on VOTS 2026 and+5.5on VOT-LT 2022. It is also the only tracker that con-
sistently succeeds in video object segmentation, scoring+1.1on MOSE v2 and+2.5on SA-V val.

keeping the backbone frozen. SAM3RL improves over SAM 3 on 11 of 12 benchmarks and ranks

that memory control should be learned rather than designed, as learned control improves even the
strongest trackers and, unlike fixed rules, remains effective across model generations.

average gain drops from 2.9 to
1.8 points. We therefore match the training rate with the strides, which requires the frame rate
to be known in advance and keeps the skipped frames out of the memory bank. The former is
rarely restrictive in practice, as the frame rate is usually available. Training at the native rate would
remove this restriction, but most decisions would then concern near-identical frames. Such a policy
could nonetheless exploit the skipped frames and improve further on high-frame-rate benchmarks.
Second, the policy controls only the seven frames in the memory bank, while the nine object pointers
are filled by a fixed rule. Learning both jointly is a natural direction for future work.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are measured on held-out external benchmarks and official challenge servers using standard metrics, independent of the PPO reward signal used for training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark metrics (Quality F-score, AUC, J&F) on held-out VOTS, VOT-LT, LaSOT, DiDi, and VOS datasets, including official evaluation servers.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: PPO training on LaSOT with reward equal to IoU tracking quality normalized by the SAM 3 default-memory baseline.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of outperforming hand-crafted heuristics and achieving state-of-the-art results across most benchmarks without inference runtime penalty are directly corroborated by standard benchmark tables, official evaluation server submissions, and throughput measurements.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation spans 12-15 diverse tracking and VOS benchmarks (including VOTS challenges, VOT-LT, LaSOT, and MOSEv2), comparing against multiple hand-crafted heuristics ported to SAM 3 as well as native SAM 2 baselines, accompanied by multi-seed ablations.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted on independent standard external tracking and segmentation test sets scored via standard toolkits and remote servers, showing consistent improvements over baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark evaluation metrics (Quality F-score, AUC, J&F) scored across held-out external benchmark sets and official challenge evaluation servers (e.g., VOTS, VOT-LT, MOSEv2, SA-V).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: PPO reinforcement learning on IoU tracking quality normalized by baseline default SAM 3 tracking performance on the LaSOT training split.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss limitations regarding fixed stride matching pre-known frame rates, the lack of full joint learning for auxiliary object pointers, and qualitative failure cases during rapid viewpoint/scale changes.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the 7-slot eviction action space, the 4-part state representation, reward normalization against a default baseline, PPO training setup on LaSOT, and strided inference matching the 5 FPS training frequency.
primary.quality_rationale: This is a rigorous, high-quality empirical study that identifies and fixes undocumented issues in foundation tracking models, systematically evaluates across standard benchmarks, and validates design choices via complete ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper presents SAM3RL (and SAM2RL), formulating memory bank control for SAM-based visual object trackers as an MDP optimized with PPO on training sequences, eliminating hand-crafted eviction heuristics.

scholarly_quality.rationale: This is a rigorous, high-quality empirical study that identifies and fixes undocumented issues in foundation tracking models, systematically evaluates across standard benchmarks, and validates design choices via complete ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly discuss limitations regarding fixed stride matching pre-known frame rates, the lack of full joint learning for auxiliary object pointers, and qualitative failure cases during rapid viewpoint/scale changes.

end-to-end models prone to failure and difficult to
adapt without massive location-specific datasets. Hence, instead of
designing a complex end-to-end pipeline for direct 3D bounding
box estimation, a low-cost, resource-efficient two-stage approach
is proposed for real-time 3D shape and orientation estimation.
The first stage utilizes any off-the-shelf, state-of-the-art method
to extract 2D camera bounding boxes and associated 3D radar
points for each road user. The proposed second stage then
processes these inputs to construct 3D oriented bounding boxes
where radar data determines 3D position, predefined templates
define size for each road user, and a tiny neural network
predicts a site-specific and optimized yaw angle. The algorithm
is successfully validated at a curved road with a junction for
pedestrians, bicycles, and cars, where it achieves25frames per
second on an NVIDIA Jetson

Training and validation forYawPredictionNetmodels for
bicycles and cars is performed using AdamW (initial learn-
ing rate10 −3, batch size1, gradient clip0.5) with a
ReduceLROnPlateauscheduler (patience 50 epochs) op-
timizingL total =L MSE(sinψ) +L MSE(cosψ). Class-specific
parameters are configured as follows:
•Bicycle:Trained for400epochs (262train /66val
samples) with weight decay0.3, requiring only73,442
trainable parameters.
•Car:Trained for100epochs (329train /76val samples)
with weight decay0.2, requiring only40,162trainable
parameters.
Owing to the lightweight architecture and minimal dataset
size required for training,YawPredictionNetis exceptionally
deployment-friendly and easily adaptable to real-time embed-
ded hardware. Furthermore, while lidar is utilized in this work,
ground-truth yaw orientation can be conveniently sourced from
alternative modalities.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final 3D bounding box errors are measured against dense LiDAR ground truth on a sequence-disjoint holdout set of 500 frames that was excluded from template tuning and YawPredictionNet training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Direct 3D metric errors (centroid, dimensions, yaw) against manually labeled LiDAR ground truth on the independent validation set.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: MSE loss on sin/cos yaw against LiDAR-derived labels for YawPredictionNet, plus manual scaling-factor and template-bound tuning on a separate development split.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported claims of real-time edge execution, resource efficiency, and improved spatial positioning over vision baselines are well supported by the experimental data and ablation studies.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The system is quantitatively evaluated on a sequence-disjoint holdout set of 500 frames containing over 1,100 road user instances against 3D LiDAR ground truth, demonstrating substantial improvements over monocular homography baselines and achieving 25 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin edge platform.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted on a sequence-disjoint holdout set of 500 frames against dense 3D LiDAR annotations not used during template tuning or yaw network training.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Direct 3D metric bounding box errors (centroid x/y/z, length, width, height, and yaw) measured against ground-truth 3D bounding boxes from dense LiDAR.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: MSE loss on trigonometric yaw representations (sinψ, cosψ) against training labels from LiDAR for YawPredictionNet, and manual parameter tuning on a separate development split for extent scaling factors.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly note that evaluation was conducted at a single roadside installation, fixed template bounds limit adaptability across vehicle sub-types, and yaw prediction models are site-optimized.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed: Stage 1 associates 2D camera detections (YOLOv11) with clustered 3D radar returns (DBSCAN), and Stage 2 computes 3D centroid and height via calibrated projections, bounds bounding box extents using class-specific geometric templates, and regresses yaw using a tiny multi-modal neural network (YawPredictionNet).
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-scoped engineering contribution with sound technical formulations, complete calibration details, thorough ablation studies, and objective benchmarking on an independent holdout set against ground truth.
primary.scoped_contribution: A resource-efficient two-stage pipeline for roadside 3D bounding box estimation and orientation of road users using an RGB camera and 3D radar, coupling geometric templates with a compact yaw prediction network.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-scoped engineering contribution with sound technical formulations, complete calibration details, thorough ablation studies, and objective benchmarking on an independent holdout set against ground truth.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly note that evaluation was conducted at a single roadside installation, fixed template bounds limit adaptability across vehicle sub-types, and yaw prediction models are site-optimized.

concerns: The paper repeatedly claims to analyze accuracy-latency-energy trade-offs and to examine quantization and runtime optimizations, but no accuracy metrics, quantization ablations, or runtime-optimization results are reported anywhere in the tables, figures, or text.

The evaluated neural network architectures are not specified: the custom 2D and 3D CNN structures, layer configurations, and implementation details are omitted, preventing reproducibility of the reported measurements.

The abstract claims a reproducible evaluation framework, but the methodology reports only three repetitions with the most stable run selected, no uncertainty or variability statistics, and no code, model definitions, or data-processing details sufficient for independent replication.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The empirical profiling data for runtime and power on the selected devices is clear, but the absence of model classification accuracy metrics, omission of network architectural specifications, and unfulfilled claims regarding quantization and runtime optimization evaluations create substantial scientific uncertainty.

specified, batch size = 1 and single-stream inference were used. 
Measurements were taken under consistent conditions. Latency is reported as the median 
inference time over repeated runs after discarding warm-up iterations. Memory usage reflects 
peak resident set size (RSS) during inference. CPU and GPU power draw were recorded through 
on-device telemetry (tegrastats for Jetson boards and vcgencmd for Raspberry Pi) at 1 Hz 
sampling, then averaged. To account for runtime variability, each experiment was repeated three 
times, and the most stable run was reported. 
This setup provides a transparent basis for comparing devices with widely different compute 
capabilities, memory budgets, and power envelopes, and lays the foundation for the 
benchmarking results reported in Section 3.2.

evidence.excerpt:
The Raspberry Pi 3 cannot function (N/F) with ResNet -50 at both 224×224 and 960×544 
resolutions due to memory and computing limitations (Table 2). In contrast, Orin achieves 
processing times of 35–50 ms (GPU power: 1150–1250 mW, memory usage: 4.5–5.5 GB), while 
Nano operates at 105–150 ms (GPU power: 600–650 mW, memory usage: 3.29–3.81 GB). When 
using the lighter 2D CNN model RMFD, all devices successfully complete inference: Orin (20–25 
ms), Nano (60–80 ms), and Raspberry Pi 3 (70–90 ms). These faster speeds come with reduced 
memory requirements approximately 2.0–2.8 GB on Orin, 1.5–2.15 GB on Nano, and 0.8–0.83 GB 
on Raspberry Pi 3. These findings highlight that model capacity (such as ResNet-50) is typically 
the primary factor that limits performance on lower-end hardware.

blocking_reasons: The paper repeatedly claims to analyze accuracy-latency-energy trade-offs and to examine quantization and runtime optimizations, but no accuracy metrics, quantization ablations, or runtime-optimization results are reported anywhere in the tables, figures, or text.

The evaluated neural network architectures are not specified: the custom 2D and 3D CNN structures, layer configurations, and implementation details are omitted, preventing reproducibility of the reported measurements.

The abstract claims a reproducible evaluation framework, but the methodology reports only three repetitions with the most stable run selected, no uncertainty or variability statistics, and no code, model definitions, or data-processing details sufficient for independent replication.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The study does not optimize against an evaluator; reported outcomes are direct hardware measurements rather than scores from a learned or automated judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Hardware profiling metrics: median inference latency, peak resident set size, and on-device CPU/GPU power telemetry.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: No model training, tuning, selection, or optimization loop is described; the study profiles pre-existing model configurations on fixed hardware.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: There is a notable mismatch between claims and evidence: the abstract and text assert examination of quantization, runtime optimizations, and speed-accuracy trade-offs, yet no model accuracy figures or quantization ablation experiments are provided in the tables or figures.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation consists solely of empirical inference measurements presented in Table 2. Crucially, task accuracy metrics (e.g., Top-1 accuracy, mAP, precision/recall) are completely absent despite repeated claims in the text about analyzing accuracy-latency-energy trade-offs.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The paper does not involve an automated tuning loop or adaptive evaluator, relying purely on hardware profiling instrumentation.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: System profiling metrics including inference latency (ms), peak resident memory (GB), and on-device telemetry power draw (mW).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Not applicable as no model training, tuning, or optimization algorithm was developed or iteratively guided in the study.

primary.limitations: The work does not adequately address its failure to report model accuracy, omit detailed architectural details of the tested networks, or explain the discrepancy between claimed quantization studies and reported results.
primary.method_assessment: While the experimental hardware profiling setup is described (single-stream batch size 1 inference, locked GPU clocks, tegrastats/vcgencmd sampling), essential architectural specifications of the evaluated neural network models (e.g., custom 2D/3D CNN layer structures and implementation details) are omitted. Claims regarding the evaluation of quantization and runtime optimizations mentioned in the abstract are not described or evidenced in the methodology.
primary.quality_rationale: The empirical profiling data for runtime and power on the selected devices is clear, but the absence of model classification accuracy metrics, omission of network architectural specifications, and unfulfilled claims regarding quantization and runtime optimization evaluations create substantial scientific uncertainty.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper presents an empirical benchmarking study profiling latency, peak resident memory, and CPU/GPU power draw across three embedded hardware platforms (NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin, Jetson Nano, and Raspberry Pi 3) executing 2D and 3D CNN architectures on gesture recognition and face mask datasets.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The empirical profiling data for runtime and power on the selected devices is clear, but the absence of model classification accuracy metrics, omission of network architectural specifications, and unfulfilled claims regarding quantization and runtime optimization evaluations create substantial scientific uncertainty.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The work does not adequately address its failure to report model accuracy, omit detailed architectural details of the tested networks, or explain the discrepancy between claimed quantization studies and reported results.

two largest DINOv3 vision transformers organize words rendered in images by
word meaning, despite being pretrained using self-supervision on images only,

brand names in the same industry group together, as do nouns from the same

We measure fourteen models (Table 1): four DINOv3 models and Web-DINO-1B, trained without
labels or captions on images alone, DINOv3-7B by self-distillation and the smaller three by distillation
from it (Siméoni et al., 2026; Fan et al., 2025); three DINOv2 models, the predecessors to DINOv3
(Oquab et al., 2024); three MAE models, trained by masked reconstruction (He et al., 2022); CLIP-B
and SigLIP2-B, trained with language supervision on image-caption pairs (Radford et al., 2021;
Tschannen et al., 2025); and an untrained ViT-B as the baseline for visual form alone. The encoder f
maps an image x to its final-layer class token, or for SigLIP2-B to the mean of its patch tokens, with
no projection head and no per-image normalization.

provide less visual overlap because they change the word width and, with centered text, shift the

Sensitivity to word form also does not predict semantic retrieval. SigLIP2-B achieves 100% top-10
accuracy for plural or base partners but only 18% for capitals, compared with 60% capital retrieval
in DINOv3-H. Conversely, the Qwen3 text encoders achieve 69–74% synonym accuracy but only

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript reports independent measurements from held-out lexical benchmarks, ImageNet visual class directions, and frozen external text and speech encoders (Qwen3, w2v-BERT), which corroborate the semantic structure found in DINOv3-H and DINOv3-7B.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Semantic retrieval benchmarks (country-capital, synonym, noun and brand category purity), word-class alignment with ImageNet visual directions, and cross-encoder alignment with frozen text and speech embeddings.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Self-supervised image-only pretraining (DINO self-distillation or masked autoencoding) and contrastive image-text or image-speech finetuning with symmetric InfoNCE loss.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims are carefully calibrated to word-level and category-level semantic structure rather than sentence comprehension or general reasoning. The manuscript appropriately notes that factual associations and category membership are substantially stronger than synonym retrieval and that broad compositional clue combinations are not supported.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations across 14 vision models demonstrate distinct emerging semantic clustering in DINOv3-H/7B across partner retrieval, brand/noun category purity, and ImageNet visual direction alignment. The reported effect sizes markedly exceed untrained baselines and smaller or earlier self-supervised models under non-parametric permutation testing.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on held-out lexical benchmarks, visual class images, and independently trained language and speech models (Qwen3, w2v-BERT).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Orthogonal semantic retrieval benchmarks (WordNet categories, country-capital pairs, synonyms) and cross-modal alignment with ImageNet class visual representations and external frozen text/speech embeddings.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pretraining self-supervision on images without language supervision (DINO self-distillation / masked autoencoding) and contrastive image-text/speech finetuning with InfoNCE loss on text-screened pairs.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including lack of evidence for compositionality, the possibility of training data containing co-occurring rendered text (e.g. from web/Instagram data), and that the origin of semantic structure remains an open mechanistic question.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology derives centered word directions by subtracting phase-scrambled matched controls across varied typography settings and background images, providing a rigorous control against low-level visual artifacts. Thorough spelling controls, including one-edit neighbor tests and length-matched permutation nulls, cleanly separate orthographic similarity from semantic organization.
primary.quality_rationale: The empirical findings are supported by disciplined experimental controls (matched visual baselines, spelling-overlap controls, background variation, and text-screened ImageNet and finetuning subsets). The claims are circumspect and fully aligned with the evidence provided.
primary.scoped_contribution: Demonstration that large self-supervised vision models (specifically DINOv3-H and DINOv3-7B) encode semantic relations among rendered written words and align with depictions of named visual categories without paired language supervision.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The empirical findings are supported by disciplined experimental controls (matched visual baselines, spelling-overlap controls, background variation, and text-screened ImageNet and finetuning subsets). The claims are circumspect and fully aligned with the evidence provided.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly acknowledge limitations including lack of evidence for compositionality, the possibility of training data containing co-occurring rendered text (e.g. from web/Instagram data), and that the origin of semantic structure remains an open mechanistic question.

Representation alignment with pretrained visual encoders improves diffusion trans-
former training but requires auxiliary encoders and extra training overhead. Recent
approaches instead exploit representations from the generative model's own varia-
tional autoencoder (V AE). However, reconstruction-oriented V AE features are not
optimized for the semantic discrimination and spatial structure needed for genera-
tive learning. We introduceCoV A(ComposedV AE Representations), a lightweight
framework that composes V AE features online into stage-wise guidance for flow-
matching training. A small latent composer is jointly trained with class supervision,
masked latent reconstruction, and horizontal-flip consistency, yielding semantically
discriminative, spatially structured dense features and sample-dependent class pos-
teriors. CoV A aligns intermediate SiT features with the composed

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard Inception-v3-based distribution metrics and Spatial LDS provide external measurement of generation quality and spatial organization, independent of the composer's training objectives.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by standard generative benchmarks on 50k samples against ImageNet reference statistics: FID, sFID, Inception Score, Precision, and Recall, plus Spatial LDS on validation latents.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The system is shaped by the flow-matching objective combined with intermediate cosine feature alignment to composer features and late-stage magnitude-corrected soft label conditioning derived from the online composer's classification, masked reconstruction, and flip-consistency losses.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of accelerated convergence and improved generation metrics without relying on large external teachers (like DINO or CLIP) are well substantiated by matched-budget comparisons and extensive control experiments. The analytical and empirical demonstration of the soft-label magnitude confound is thoroughly validated through directional decompositions and null-centered scaling baselines.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The framework is evaluated systematically on class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 across multiple SiT model scales (B/2, L/2, XL/2) using established standard metrics including FID, sFID, Inception Score, Precision, and Recall. The paper features comprehensive ablation studies isolating the composer objectives, stopping schedules, and the magnitude confound in soft conditioning.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Standard image distribution metrics (FID, sFID, IS, Precision, Recall) evaluated externally via standard Inception-v3 features on generated samples.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard generative benchmarking on 50k samples using reference dataset distributions: Frechet Inception Distance (FID), sFID, Inception Score, and Precision/Recall, alongside Spatial LDS on validation latents.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Flow-matching loss combined with intermediate cosine feature alignment and late-stage magnitude-corrected soft label conditioning derived from the online composer's classification and MIM objectives.

primary.limitations: The work explicitly notes the stage sensitivity of representation alignment and soft label conditioning, requiring thresholded scheduling. Evaluations are scoped primarily to class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 under SiT backbones.
primary.method_assessment: The method is clearly formulated with formal descriptions of the composer loss, cosine feature alignment, alignment early stopping, and magnitude-corrected soft label conditioning to decouple directional semantic interpolation from embedding attenuation. Experimental protocols, architectural details, and hyperparameters are thoroughly documented.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript provides a well-scoped, rigorously tested contribution to diffusion transformer training dynamics. The experiments thoroughly investigate the proposed mechanisms with appropriate controls and ablations, meeting the standard for inclusion.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces CoVA, an online training scheme for flow-matching diffusion transformers that reorganizes VAE representations using an auxiliary latent composer trained with classification, masked reconstruction, and flip-consistency objectives. CoVA performs intermediate feature alignment early in training, transitions to magnitude-corrected soft label conditioning using the detached composer posterior late in training, and discards all auxiliary parameters at inference.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript provides a well-scoped, rigorously tested contribution to diffusion transformer training dynamics. The experiments thoroughly investigate the proposed mechanisms with appropriate controls and ablations, meeting the standard for inclusion.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The work explicitly notes the stage sensitivity of representation alignment and soft label conditioning, requiring thresholded scheduling. Evaluations are scoped primarily to class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 under SiT backbones.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Full downstream retraining on established external benchmarks (ACDC, Dark Zurich, WXSOD, CSOD10K) shows consistent gains over uncurated and baseline-curated sets, and region-level cRDG rankings correlate with independently measured per-region retraining utility.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark metrics on real adverse-condition and SOD test sets (mIoU on ACDC/Dark Zurich, MAE/F-beta/E-measure/S-measure on WXSOD/CSOD10K), plus per-region retraining gains on real targets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Short K-step treatment and clean-control probe losses on split source data, used to compute cRDG and rank degradation-severity regions for selection.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding the non-monotonic nature of training utility, the shift in correctable bands across models/budgets, and CuRB's performance gains over uncurated twins and baseline valuation metrics are directly supported by benchmark metrics and correlation with ground-truth retraining gains.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluations are comprehensive across semantic segmentation (Cityscapes to ACDC, Dark Zurich) and salient object detection (WXSOD, CSOD10K) under strict budget-matched protocols. The paper isolates the effect of curation against multiple data-selection baselines, tests plug-in compatibility across several generators, verifies compute tradeoffs, and performs informative ablations.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Full downstream retraining evaluated on established external benchmarks (ACDC, Dark Zurich, WXSOD, CSOD10K) demonstrates consistent performance gains over uncurated and baseline-curated sets.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark test evaluation metrics (mIoU on real adverse conditions like ACDC/Dark Zurich, and MAE/F-beta/E-measure/S-measure on real SOD datasets).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Short K-step treatment and control probe training losses on split source data using synthetic degradation twins versus weak photometric augmentations.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently document limitations, including reliance on single-run evaluations for final training, residual drift near gate thresholds, reliance on cross-family transfer for completely novel degradation types, and probe budget heuristics.
primary.method_assessment: The method mathematically isolates degradation-specific reducible error from clean forgetting and generic optimization progress using cross-fitted matched control probes. The candidate pool generation, structural DINOv2 validity gating, budget allocation, and clean-harm constraint are well specified.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-controlled experimental setup addressing a genuine confound in synthetic data selection. The mathematical formulation is clear, baselines are fairly adapted under matched budgets, and empirical analyses thoroughly probe underlying mechanisms.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces the controlled Reducible Degradation Gap (cRDG) and the Curation of Reducible Bands (CuRB) framework, which scores synthetic degradation-severity regions via budget-matched short probes relative to a clean-control stream, curating synthetic data for dense prediction without target-domain exposure.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a rigorous, well-controlled experimental setup addressing a genuine confound in synthetic data selection. The mathematical formulation is clear, baselines are fairly adapted under matched budgets, and empirical analyses thoroughly probe underlying mechanisms.

The performance of all model configurations and their fine-tuned variants was evaluated using the F1 score. 21
Predicted and reference instances were matched using an IoU threshold of 0.5. The F1 score was computed for
each test patch and then averaged across all test patches. It was calculated as:
F1 = 2TP
2TP + FP + FN,
where TP, FP, and FN denote true-positive, false-positive, and false-negative nuclei instances, respectively.
The F1 score was used as the primary evaluation metric because it jointly accounts for false-positive and false-
negative predictions.

by
combining Medium and Hard annotations. Cellpose 3.0 achieved its highest F1 score using the complete Easy plus
Medium plus Hard dataset. In contrast, Hard-only fine-tuning was optimal for Cellpose-DINO and LSP-DETR.
Overall, seven of the nine best-performing strategies included the newly annotated Medium data. Although
Easy + Hard fine-tuning improved performance over the corresponding baseline for eight of the nine model
configurations, it was not the optimal strategy for any model once Medium-containing strategies were included
in the comparison. These results indicate that the newly annotated Medium cases provided complementary
kidney-specific supervision beyond the previously available Easy and Hard data, although the optimal data
composition remained model dependent.

We observed substantial differences in the magnitude of improvement across models. StarDist showed the
largest absolute gain, increasing from 0.7380 to 0.8332 with Medium-only fine-tuning, corresponding to an
improvement of 0.0952. Cellpose-SAM showed the second-largest gain of 0.0841. Cellpose 3.0 and Cellpose-

[HIPT-256], LSP-DETR, CellViT++ [Virchow], CellViT [SAM-H], and PathoSAM. These results show that the
effect of human-in-the-loop data enrichment varied according to the model configuration and its baseline.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The headline F1 gains are measured on a fixed 185-patch expert-annotated hold-out set explicitly excluded from training, validation, pseudo-label generation, and data enrichment.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Instance-level F1 at IoU 0.5 against expert ground-truth annotations on the independent 185-patch hold-out test set.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Fine-tuning supervision from Easy pseudo-labels and expert Medium/Hard annotations via task segmentation loss with AdamW.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that Medium annotations offer complementary supervision and that optimal fine-tuning compositions are model-dependent are directly backed by the reported benchmark metrics and qualitative comparisons.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation systematically assesses 63 fine-tuning experiments on an independent hold-out test set of 185 expert-annotated kidney pathology patches using instance-level F1 score at IoU 0.5, with clear baseline comparisons.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations were performed on a separate, fixed hold-out test set of 185 expert-annotated patches completely excluded from training, validation, and pseudo-label selection.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Instance-level F1 score computed at an IoU threshold of 0.5 against an independent hold-out test set of 185 expert-annotated kidney pathology patches.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Fine-tuning was supervised on varying mixtures of foundation-model pseudo-labels (Easy) and expert manual ground-truth annotations (Medium and Hard) using task segmentation loss via AdamW.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently acknowledge limitations, including restriction to renal pathology, a single 185-patch hold-out test set, predefined non-tuned oversampling weights, and reliance on single training runs without stochastic variance bounds.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the curation of Easy pseudo-labels, Hard failure annotations, and 860 newly annotated Medium patches, alongside weighted oversampling to balance source contributions during fine-tuning across nine distinct model architectures.
primary.quality_rationale: The study offers a well-scoped, rigorously conducted benchmark addressing an established open question regarding human-in-the-loop data efficiency in computational pathology, providing reproducible experimental details and clear boundaries.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper provides an empirical evaluation and fine-tuning study investigating whether adding expert annotations of intermediate-difficulty ('Medium') renal pathology patches improves cell nuclei instance segmentation across nine foundation model configurations under seven adaptation data mixtures.

posterior mean µϕ(s) and inserted into the BO observation set together with its penalized composite score.
