which we follow without modification. The training took 32 hours on 8 A100 GPUs.
The model achieves state-of-the-art top-1 accuracy on the ImageNet validation set among models trained
with the standard UniNAS protocol (Table 1). Compared to accuracy reported by other zero- and one-shot
approaches on the same task (Table 2), our method also clearly discovers highest-scoring architecture for the
smallest GPU cost, demonstrating that the combination of a well-structured latent space with BO-guided

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The selected architecture is trained from scratch on ImageNet-1K and fine-tuned on MS-COCO and ADE20K, with reported top-1 accuracy, AP, and mIoU compared against established baselines.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Ground-truth validation accuracy after full training on ImageNet-1K and downstream task metrics on MS-COCO and ADE20K.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Scalarized zero-shot proxy scores from whitened VKDNW components with a parameter-count penalty.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of achieving competitive zero-shot NAS performance (81.51% top-1 ImageNet-1K at ~27M parameters) and cross-task generalization align well with the empirical training results and comparative tables.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The authors evaluate the single top-selected architecture by fully training it on ImageNet-1K under the standard UniNAS recipe, transferring it to COCO object detection/segmentation and ADE20K semantic segmentation, and providing component ablations covering latent space, prefix encoding, and proxy scalarization.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Full training and standard task metric evaluation (top-1 classification accuracy, AP, and mIoU) on standard benchmarks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Actual ground-truth validation accuracy following complete training from scratch on ImageNet-1K, MS-COCO, and ADE20K.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Scalarized zero-shot training-free proxy scores (whitened VKDNW multi-dimensional components) penalized by parameter deviation.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge that the proxy scalarizer covariance is frozen after initialization rather than adaptively recalibrated, and that latent decoding requires retry perturbation for occasional invalid shape matching.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing the 20-node compound prefix grammar, the graph convolutional encoder and autoregressive transformer decoder with soft-DTW loss, the multi-proxy whitening scalarization, and budget-penalized GP-based Bayesian optimization.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clearly motivated, novel system that scales BO to expressive NAS spaces via a grammar-constrained latent space, with robust full-training verification on standard vision benchmarks and solid ablations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces a Bayesian Optimization approach for zero-shot neural architecture search over large-scale spaces by learning a continuous latent space with a VAE operating on a prefix encoding of architecture graphs, coupled with a Mahalanobis-whitened proxy scalarization.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clearly motivated, novel system that scales BO to expressive NAS spaces via a grammar-constrained latent space, with robust full-training verification on standard vision benchmarks and solid ablations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge that the proxy scalarizer covariance is frozen after initialization rather than adaptively recalibrated, and that latent decoding requires retry perturbation for occasional invalid shape matching.

concerns: The manuscript reports only single-run results on a single 10% test split without confidence intervals, standard deviations, repeated trials, or statistical testing, so the margin between RF-DETR Medium (mAP@50 0.869) and the best YOLO variants (0.834-0.841) is not established as statistically robust.

The augmentation pipeline is described as expanding the dataset to 3,385 images before the 70/20/10 split is stated, leaving potential train/test leakage from augmented copies of test images unresolved.
The 'YOLOv8m combined with CNN layers' ensemble is described only vaguely, with no architectural detail or training procedure sufficient to reproduce or interpret its reported 0.841 mAP.

The paper's broad claim that transformer-based detectors provide higher accuracy and stronger generalization than convolution-based approaches is based on a single small custom dataset with severe class imbalance (e.g., 107 Al-Qaeda images) and no external benchmark or out-of-distribution evaluation.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: While the paper provides a straightforward comparative study on a specialized destructive visual content dataset, the technical contributions are limited to dataset assembly and standard fine-tuning of existing models. Given ambiguities around augmentation pipeline splitting, single-run evaluation without error bounds, and limited algorithmic novelty, the study's scientific rigor remains uncertain.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The manuscript reports only single-run results on a single 10% test split without confidence intervals, standard deviations, repeated trials, or statistical testing, so the margin between RF-DETR Medium (mAP@50 0.869) and the best YOLO variants (0.834-0.841) is not established as statistically robust.

The augmentation pipeline is described as expanding the dataset to 3,385 images before the 70/20/10 split is stated, leaving potential train/test leakage from augmented copies of test images unresolved.
The 'YOLOv8m combined with CNN layers' ensemble is described only vaguely, with no architectural detail or training procedure sufficient to reproduce or interpret its reported 0.841 mAP.

The paper's broad claim that transformer-based detectors provide higher accuracy and stronger generalization than convolution-based approaches is based on a single small custom dataset with severe class imbalance (e.g., 107 Al-Qaeda images) and no external benchmark or out-of-distribution evaluation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The final evaluation uses objective ground-truth metrics on a held-out test split rather than a learned or model-generated evaluator, so no circularity is present.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Deterministic Precision, Recall, and mAP@0.5 computed against manually annotated ground-truth bounding boxes on the held-out test split.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised bounding-box regression and classification losses minimized via AdamW during training of the detection models.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that RF-DETR Medium outperforms convolutional architectures on this domain are supported by the reported single-split mAP@50 numbers, but broader claims regarding transformer superiority and real-time operational safety readiness are moderately overstated given small sample sizes for certain classes (e.g., Hamas, Al-Qaeda) and lack of out-of-distribution testing.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation reports standard precision, recall, and mAP@50 metrics across models and classes on a 10% test split. However, the manuscript does not report confidence intervals, standard deviations across multiple runs, or formal statistical testing, leaving uncertainty around whether the 0.869 mAP of RF-DETR vs 0.834-0.841 for YOLO models represents a statistically robust margin rather than single-run variance.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The final evaluation relies on an objective ground-truth metric (mAP@50) evaluated on a held-out test split rather than an adaptive, synthetic, or model-based evaluator.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard deterministic object detection metrics (Precision, Recall, mAP@0.5) computed against ground-truth bounding box annotations on the test split.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised bounding-box regression and classification loss functions minimized via the AdamW optimizer during training.

primary.limitations: The authors acknowledge class imbalance and limited sample sizes for specific extremist symbols, but omit discussion of potential data leakage during augmentation, lack of repeated trials, and the absence of external benchmark evaluations.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology compiles 2,068 images via keyword scraping, annotates them via Roboflow into COCO format, expands the dataset via augmentation to 3,385 images, and trains existing standard detection models under standard training configurations (50 epochs, batch size 16, AdamW). However, methodological descriptions regarding the exact structure and implementation of the 'YOLOv8m combined with CNN layers' ensemble remain vague, and augmentation appears to have been applied before or without clear isolation from dataset splitting.
primary.quality_rationale: While the paper provides a straightforward comparative study on a specialized destructive visual content dataset, the technical contributions are limited to dataset assembly and standard fine-tuning of existing models. Given ambiguities around augmentation pipeline splitting, single-run evaluation without error bounds, and limited algorithmic novelty, the study's scientific rigor remains uncertain.
primary.scoped_contribution: A benchmark and comparative evaluation of off-the-shelf object detection architectures (YOLOv8 variants, YOLOv11s, YOLOv8m+CNN, and RF-DETR Medium) on a custom 11-class dataset of destructive visual content (weapons, blood, and extremist organization symbols).

scholarly_quality.rationale: While the paper provides a straightforward comparative study on a specialized destructive visual content dataset, the technical contributions are limited to dataset assembly and standard fine-tuning of existing models. Given ambiguities around augmentation pipeline splitting, single-run evaluation without error bounds, and limited algorithmic novelty, the study's scientific rigor remains uncertain.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors acknowledge class imbalance and limited sample sizes for specific extremist symbols, but omit discussion of potential data leakage during augmentation, lack of repeated trials, and the absence of external benchmark evaluations.

citation: Improving Image Classification Performance with Modern Data Augmentation and Vision Transformer. Abderrahmane Bouidi, Lahcen Oughdir. 2026-10-02. https://doi.org/10.48084/etasr.20583
publication_status_evidence: OpenAlex records a published journal location: Engineering Technology & Applied Science Research. Peer review inferred from venue metadata, not independently verified.
relevance_reason: Studies object-detection architecture, training, or evaluation.

concerns: The manuscript contains a major internal contradiction: Section III describes a hybrid CNN with VGG-style convolution layers, three inception modules, and three residual blocks, while Table I and Figure 3 describe a standard ViT-Base pipeline with 16x16 patches and no explanation of how these architectures relate.

The evaluation is too weak to support the headline claims: only four configurations are compared over 20 epochs on CIFAR-10, with no standard deviations, no repeated runs, no statistical testing, and no comparison against the self-supervised methods the abstract claims to outperform.

The robustness claims are underspecified: CIFAR-10-C is mentioned in the discussion, but the manuscript does not report how corrupted images were generated, which corruptions or severities were used, or any quantitative CIFAR-10-C results.
The abstract claims higher accuracy against existing self-supervised methods, but no self-supervised baseline is trained or evaluated anywhere in the paper.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: Due to major methodological discrepancies in model definition and an extremely limited, underspecified evaluation protocol, scientific quality and validity remain highly uncertain.

accuracy. The model is trained and evaluated on the  CIFAR-10 dataset, demonstrating higher accuracy 
against existing self-supervised methods.

blocking_reasons: The manuscript contains a major internal contradiction: Section III describes a hybrid CNN with VGG-style convolution layers, three inception modules, and three residual blocks, while Table I and Figure 3 describe a standard ViT-Base pipeline with 16x16 patches and no explanation of how these architectures relate.

The evaluation is too weak to support the headline claims: only four configurations are compared over 20 epochs on CIFAR-10, with no standard deviations, no repeated runs, no statistical testing, and no comparison against the self-supervised methods the abstract claims to outperform.

The robustness claims are underspecified: CIFAR-10-C is mentioned in the discussion, but the manuscript does not report how corrupted images were generated, which corruptions or severities were used, or any quantitative CIFAR-10-C results.
The abstract claims higher accuracy against existing self-supervised methods, but no self-supervised baseline is trained or evaluated anywhere in the paper.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The reported accuracy and robustness are computed from CIFAR-10 test predictions, and no evidence indicates the test metric was used to optimize the model.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Top-1 accuracy and robustness ratio on CIFAR-10 test data.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training loss with AdamW on CIFAR-10 training data.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding superior accuracy against self-supervised methods or state-of-the-art vision pipelines are unsubstantiated by the narrow 4-row comparison table with underspecified models trained for only 20 epochs.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation compares basic setups across just 20 epochs on CIFAR-10, with unclear baseline specifications and minimal details on how corruption robustness (e.g. CIFAR-10-C) was generated or tested despite being mentioned in discussion.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted using standard classification metric calculations on test splits.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Top-1 classification accuracy and perturbed accuracy ratio on CIFAR-10 test splits.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised cross-entropy loss with AdamW optimization on CIFAR-10.

primary.limitations: The study does not address the contradiction between the described inception/residual architecture and the ViT pipeline, lacks standard baselines or variance estimates, and does not provide comprehensive ablation.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology contains severe structural inconsistencies: Section III describes a hybrid CNN model with inception and residual blocks, whereas Table I and Figure 3 present standard ViT-Base with image patch tokens and Multi-Level DA without explaining how the two descriptions connect.
primary.quality_rationale: Due to major methodological discrepancies in model definition and an extremely limited, underspecified evaluation protocol, scientific quality and validity remain highly uncertain.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript evaluates combining Vision Transformers with data augmentation techniques (termed MDAViT) on CIFAR-10 image classification and robustness under perturbations.

We begin by considering feed-forward reconstruction (Wang et al., 2024; 2025), where a multi-view
transformer directly predicts scene geometry from a sequence of images. We consider three eval-
uation settings of increasing computational complexity (i) train only the pose and depth head, (ii)
train a transformer, and (iii) finetune the full model with new heads. We train on a large collection
of labeled 3D datasets using 4 H200 GPUs for each experiment and report the results in Tab. 1
together with training curves in Fig. 7. Poincar3 shows substantially improved performance, espe-
cially on camera pose estimation, compared to all existing models. Furthermore, initializing from
the Poincar3 weights allows for rapid finetuning, achieving an AUC@30◦ of 65.0%+ on RE10K af-
ter only 10K steps with a low learning rate. Further details can be found in Sec. E in the Appendix.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Headline outcomes are measured with ground-truth camera poses, depths, and correspondences on held-out benchmarks such as RE10K, ScanNet++, MegaDepth, ETH3D, DTU, ScanNet, and NAVI, which are independent of the self-distillation training objective.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Ground-truth geometric metrics on held-out benchmarks, including pose AUC, point cloud error, normal consistency, and PCK correspondence accuracy.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Multi-view self-distillation loss combining masked patch distillation, global CLS cross-entropy against an EMA teacher with extra views, and KoLeo regularization.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding superior geometric transfer over RGB-reconstruction multi-view SSL and single-view self-distillation are well supported by quantitative improvements across standard pose, point cloud, and correspondence metrics. The paper explicitly notes trade-offs, showing that prioritizing multi-view geometry leads to lower performance on semantic recognition tasks.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation is extensive across diverse benchmarks and tasks, comparing frozen and finetuned backbones on feed-forward reconstruction (RE10K, ScanNet++, MegaDepth, ETH3D, DTU), zero-shot multi-view correspondence (ScanNet, NAVI), and SE(3) adapter probing. Meaningful ablations validate each component (image-level loss, teacher extra views, and removing local crops) against prior SSL baselines (MuM, Muskie, DINOv3).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted using ground-truth geometric annotations (camera poses, depths, and 3D point correspondences) on held-out benchmark datasets completely separate from the self-supervised pretraining objective.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: External ground-truth 3D geometric metrics across established benchmarks: pose AUC on RE10K/ScanNet++/MegaDepth, point cloud error/normal consistency on ETH3D/DTU, and PCK correspondence matching on ScanNet and NAVI.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Multi-view self-distillation loss comprising masked patch distillation, global CLS cross-entropy against an EMA teacher seeing additional views, and KoLeo regularization.

primary.limitations: The authors identify limitations transparently, including reduced semantic classification performance compared to DINOv3, hyperparameter sensitivity inherent to self-distillation frameworks, and heuristic/handcrafted frame selection from training videos.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is described thoroughly with explicit objectives, architecture details, and pseudocode combining masked patch-level distillation, image-level global CLS distillation, and extra unmasked context views for the teacher network. Implementation details, training schedules, hyperparameters, and stability regularizations (Sinkhorn-Knopp, KoLeo) are adequately documented.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-motivated conceptual advance moving multi-view SSL away from appearance-entangling RGB pixel reconstruction to self-distillation. The system design is validated with thorough experiments, consistent baselines, clear ablation studies, and transparent reporting of limitations.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Poincar3, a multi-view self-supervised representation learning method utilizing self-distillation rather than RGB reconstruction across views. It demonstrates emergent 3D geometric capabilities—such as zero-shot multi-view correspondence, SE(3) camera motion decodability, and strong feed-forward 3D reconstruction initialization—trained from scratch on unlabeled video and image collections.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clear, well-motivated conceptual advance moving multi-view SSL away from appearance-entangling RGB pixel reconstruction to self-distillation. The system design is validated with thorough experiments, consistent baselines, clear ablation studies, and transparent reporting of limitations.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors identify limitations transparently, including reduced semantic classification performance compared to DINOv3, hyperparameter sensitivity inherent to self-distillation frameworks, and heuristic/handcrafted frame selection from training videos.

concerns: The manuscript reports no statistical significance testing or uncertainty quantification for the claimed performance gains, and several headline improvements are small (e.g., HOTA +1.550, MOTA +1.368 in open systems), leaving the robustness of the reported advantages unestablished.

The evaluation independence of the headline outcome is not established: the manuscript does not report whether the threshold values and heuristic parameters were tuned on the same test benchmarks used to report final results, and no held-out validation or independent calibration is described.

The paper contains a mathematical error in the IoU definition, where the union and intersection terms are reversed in Equation 3, undermining confidence in the methodological rigor of the described architecture.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The paper provides an adequately scoped and well-executed experimental comparison of an architectural refinement to an established tracking baseline. Controlled testing on multiple standard datasets and across multiple thresholds provides solid empirical support for the claimed gains.

To effectively resolve the issue of erroneous ID reassig-
nation, a merging step is implemented for screening
all new tracklets. This relies upon the logic that for
a system with a fixed track count for which all tracks
are currently present, additional tracklets that overlap
with existing trajectories likely represents repeat detec-
tions of the same objects. Consequently, new tracks
that meet these criteria are immediately merged into
the existing same-class tracks with which they over-
lap, thus preventing the assignation of a new ID to
an established track, even if the former exhibits higher
detection confidence. This process is governed by the
following equation:
M = 𝐼𝑜𝑈 (𝑇existing, 𝐷new) ≥ 𝜏 merge (6)
In which M represents the decision to merge a new
detection 𝐷new into an existing track 𝑇existing, depen-
dent upon their combined IoU meeting or exceeding
the threshold 𝜏merge.

evidence.excerpt:
I utilise six standardised benchmarks to evaluate the
performance of ByteTraX in comparison to that of the
ByteTrack baseline. These encompass a diversity of
tracking scenarios, target types, and motion patterns,
while providing detailed ground truth annotations for
both bounding boxes and track identities. The first
three of these—GMOT-40 [ 16], SportsMOT [ 18], and
DeepSea-MOT [ 21]—represent open systems in which
tracks can enter and leave the frame (Fig. 2a); while
the latter three—LC-MOT [ 17], TeamTrack [ 19], and
DAMUNT [20]—are closed systems in which all tracks
remain in view across videos (Fig. 2b). While the vast
scope of potential real-world deployments cannot fea-
sibly be encompassed by benchmarking alone [ 30], the
aforementioned datasets allow for relative performance
comparisons across widely divergent tracking scenarios.

evidence.excerpt:
As the principle aim of ByteTraX is not to challenge
the state-of-the-art, but to improve upon the widely-
established ByteTrack baseline, I focus my comparisons
on these two architectures exclusively. Results are
broadly divided into those from open and closed sys-
tem benchmarks, and all assessments utilise the same
upstream YOLO26 models across tracking algorithms
to ensure parity.
Open System Benchmarks. When considering open sys-
tem benchmarks, ByteTraX substantially outperforms
ByteTrack in overall tracking accuracy and speed,
achieving a mean increase in HOTA of 1.550, MOTA
of 1.368, and FPS of 5.170 (Fig. 3a, Table 2). This is
driven by markedly enhanced identity preservation, re-
flected in an IDF1 score increase of 2.575, and crucially,
a >36% reduction in identity switches, with mean
IDSW dropping from 91 to 58, and excess IDs from
1013 to 447 (Fig. 3a, Fig. 4, Table 2).

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The manuscript reports no statistical significance testing or uncertainty quantification for the claimed performance gains, and several headline improvements are small (e.g., HOTA +1.550, MOTA +1.368 in open systems), leaving the robustness of the reported advantages unestablished.

The evaluation independence of the headline outcome is not established: the manuscript does not report whether the threshold values and heuristic parameters were tuned on the same test benchmarks used to report final results, and no held-out validation or independent calibration is described.

The paper contains a mathematical error in the IoU definition, where the union and intersection terms are reversed in Equation 3, undermining confidence in the methodological rigor of the described architecture.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript does not report any measurement independent of the benchmark test sets used for the reported results, such as held-out validation, statistical significance testing, or independent human assessment.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard MOT metrics (HOTA, MOTA, IDF1, IDSW, FPS) computed via TrackEval on the benchmark test splits against ground-truth annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Threshold adjustments and heuristic rules for association, reconnection, and merging, with parameters selected across detection confidence thresholds of 0.25, 0.50, and 0.75 on the same benchmark datasets.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding identity switch reduction, accuracy improvements, and processing speed enhancements align directly with the tabulated results across benchmarks [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0003, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0038, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0048]. The author appropriately positions the work as an enhancement of ByteTrack rather than claiming state-of-the-art across all MOT methods [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0041, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0050].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation rigorously compares ByteTraX against the baseline ByteTrack across six distinct benchmarks representing both open and closed tracking environments [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0030, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0038, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0048]. It employs standard multi-object tracking metrics (HOTA, MOTA, IDF1, IDSW) and hardware-controlled runtime speed measurements across varying confidence thresholds [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0033, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0038, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0039].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on ground-truth benchmark test annotations and standardized external evaluation toolkits (TrackEval) across six public datasets [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0030, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0039].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard multi-object tracking metrics (HOTA, MOTA, IDF1, IDSW) computed via TrackEval on independent test splits against ground-truth trajectories [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0033, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0037, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0039].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Pre-determined threshold adjustments and heuristic rules defined for association, reconnection, and merging, coupled with upstream YOLO26 models trained on the training splits [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0019, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0024, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0037].

primary.limitations: The manuscript explicitly distinguishes open versus closed tracking environments, noting that reconnection and merging heuristics rely on fixed track counts and are unsuitable for general open systems [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0027, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0038]. It also notes that comparisons are restricted specifically to ByteTrack [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0037, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0041].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is described mathematically and procedurally, detailing the elimination of confidence score prioritization, the IoU matching modification, and the closed-system heuristics [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0019, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0021, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0024, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0026]. The upstream detector and training/test splits are clearly standardized across systems [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0037].
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides an adequately scoped and well-executed experimental comparison of an architectural refinement to an established tracking baseline. Controlled testing on multiple standard datasets and across multiple thresholds provides solid empirical support for the claimed gains.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript proposes ByteTraX, an adaptation of the ByteTrack multi-object tracking architecture that removes two-stage score binning, applies lenient IoU association thresholds, and adds optional track reconnection and merging heuristics for closed-system tracking [Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0002, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0019, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0021, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0024, Ee6822e79e5bc6372-B0026].

To address this limitation, we proposeEviSplat, which keeps individual observation features avail-
able for query-dependent selection. Using LaGa's class-agnostic grouping (Cen et al., 2025b), EviS-
plat organizes these features into instance observation banks (Fig. 1, bottom). Since different obser-

tribution for each Gaussian to capture its locally supported evidence. Given a query, query-guided
evidence aggregation forms an instance-level score from the most relevant observations and refines

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Benchmark metrics use external ground-truth mask and point annotations that are separate from the training loss and query-time scoring.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established by mIoU and mAcc against ground-truth human annotations on LERF-OVS, 3D-OVS, and ScanNet.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The evidence field is trained by cross-entropy against empirical prototype distributions derived from unsupervised clustering of multi-view CLIP features, with no text queries or label vocabulary involved.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of superior open-vocabulary segmentation performance and the benefit of retaining multi-view evidence over pre-query consolidation are solidly backed by empirical gains across benchmarks (e.g., 70.7 vs 63.6 baseline mIoU on LERF-OVS) and detailed ablations.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation spans standard open-vocabulary benchmarks including LERF-OVS, 3D-OVS, and ScanNet under both rendered-view and 3D point-level protocols. It provides extensive controlled component analyses, seed variance reporting, and ablation of storage and perturbation sensitivity.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations rely on established ground-truth 2D mask and 3D point annotations that are entirely external and separate from the training loss.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard benchmark evaluation metrics (mIoU and mAcc) computed against ground-truth human annotations on LERF-OVS, 3D-OVS, and ScanNet.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss against empirical prototype distributions derived from unsupervised clustering of multi-view CLIP embeddings, completely independent of test text queries and annotations.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly acknowledge dependencies on source 2D mask segmentations and frozen CLIP representations, as well as limitations in handling complex attribute combinations and spatial relationships.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is clearly articulated, outlining instance observation banking, Gaussian-to-observation association weighting, prototype codebook construction, and evidence-distribution distillation via latent vectors. Query-guided aggregation is rigorously formalized with fixed-mass prototype scoring and reliability-weighted fusion.
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides a well-motivated architectural enhancement to 3D Gaussian Splatting for open-vocabulary tasks with thorough ablation studies, transparent implementation details, and solid benchmarking against state-of-the-art baselines.
primary.scoped_contribution: EviSplat introduces an open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian Splatting framework that preserves individual multi-view observation features in instance banks and learns a Gaussian-local evidence field, dynamically aggregating query-relevant visual evidence at query time.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The paper provides a well-motivated architectural enhancement to 3D Gaussian Splatting for open-vocabulary tasks with thorough ablation studies, transparent implementation details, and solid benchmarking against state-of-the-art baselines.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly acknowledge dependencies on source 2D mask segmentations and frozen CLIP representations, as well as limitations in handling complex attribute combinations and spatial relationships.

citation: Cloud-Based Facial Expression Recognition Using Squeeze Vision Transformer. S. Al-Darraji, A. J. Jalil. 2026-09-26. https://doi.org/10.26437/2pdqpg59
publication_status_evidence: OpenAlex records a published journal location: African Journal Of Applied Research. Peer review inferred from venue metadata, not independently verified.
relevance_reason: Studies visual backbones or vision-transformer architecture.

concerns: The paper's central title and abstract frame the work as a cloud-based system using a Squeeze Vision Transformer, but the actually trained and evaluated pipeline is a standard ImageNet-pretrained ViT-small backbone; the dedicated squeeze-layer local-global fusion module is explicitly stated to be part of the formulated architecture only and not the evaluated model [E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].

The cloud claim is not empirically substantiated: the cloud component was storage only, and no serving latency, throughput, memory, or cost measurements are reported, so the practical implication of cloud/edge-cloud suitability is not established by the evidence [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0011, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].

The evaluation lacks direct comparative baselines under identical splits or setups, repeated runs, or statistical dispersion, leaving the reported accuracy pattern without a controlled reference for the claimed efficiency-accuracy trade-off [E31e576869c0657c4-B0026, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050].
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The contribution is modest, essentially consisting of fine-tuning an off-the-shelf ViT-small model on three legacy datasets. The gap between the formulated squeeze-fusion method and the actually evaluated architecture, combined with the lack of direct baseline comparisons and missing cloud/edge empirical runtime evaluations despite the paper's central title and theme, warrants an uncertain assessment.

Purpose: This paper presents and evaluates a cloud -oriented facial expression 
recognition (FER) system built on a compact, squeeze -style Vision Transformer, and 
assesses its suitability as an accurate , resource-efficient modelling layer for cloud and 
edge-cloud deployment. 
Design/Methodology/Approach: A pretrained ViT -small-patch16-224 backbone is 
fine-tuned for seven-class facial expression classification (angry, disgust, fear, happy, 
neutral, sad, and surprise). Images from three benchmark datasets (CK+, JAFFE, and 
KDEF) are preprocessed by resizing, converting to grayscale, converting to tensors, 
normalising, and expanding channels. The model is trained with cross-entropy loss and 
the Adam optimiser over ten epochs. Performance is assessed using accuracy, loss, per-
class precision, recall, and F1-score, macro-averaged metrics, and confusion matrices. 
Research

cloud-serving latency, throughput, and cost have not yet been tested.  
Findings: The model attains 97.5% accuracy on CK+ (macro F1 of 0.956), 95.0% on 
JAFFE (macro F1 of 0.946), and 86.1% on KDEF (macro F1 of 0.857). Accuracy is 
highest on the tightly controlled CK+ and JAFFE datasets and lower on the more 
heterogeneous KDEF, with Fear and Disgust the most frequently confused expressions 
across all three datasets.

transformers can act as an accurate and computationally efficient modelling layer for 
cloud and edge -cloud FER services. They reduce the computational complexity and

Evaluation Metrics 
To measure the performance of this work, various metrics are used. These metrics are 
accuracy, training and validation loss, precision, recall, F1 -score, and the confusion

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The paper's central title and abstract frame the work as a cloud-based system using a Squeeze Vision Transformer, but the actually trained and evaluated pipeline is a standard ImageNet-pretrained ViT-small backbone; the dedicated squeeze-layer local-global fusion module is explicitly stated to be part of the formulated architecture only and not the evaluated model [E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].

The cloud claim is not empirically substantiated: the cloud component was storage only, and no serving latency, throughput, memory, or cost measurements are reported, so the practical implication of cloud/edge-cloud suitability is not established by the evidence [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0011, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].

The evaluation lacks direct comparative baselines under identical splits or setups, repeated runs, or statistical dispersion, leaving the reported accuracy pattern without a controlled reference for the claimed efficiency-accuracy trade-off [E31e576869c0657c4-B0026, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The final outcome is measured with objective dataset ground-truth labels on held-out test splits, not with a learned or automated surrogate judge.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Accuracy, macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score computed against ground-truth categorical labels on the held-out 30% test sets [E31e576869c0657c4-B0047, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss with the Adam optimizer over ten epochs on 70% training splits, with the checkpoint selected by highest test accuracy [E31e576869c0657c4-B0046, E31e576869c0657c4-B0047].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding cloud-based deployment and suitability are decoupled from the evidence, as the paper only conducts offline training and testing where the cloud aspect was restricted to cloud-hosted file storage [E31e576869c0657c4-B0011, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065]. The evaluated model is standard ViT-small fine-tuning rather than the novel hybrid SqueezeViT fusion architecture formulated in the methodology section [E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation reports standard offline classification metrics (accuracy, macro F1, precision, recall) across 70/30 train/test splits of three standard laboratory datasets [E31e576869c0657c4-B0026, E31e576869c0657c4-B0029, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050]. No comparative baselines are benchmarked under identical splits or setups, no statistical dispersion or repeated runs are provided, and no cloud runtime benchmarks (latency, memory footprint, throughput) are measured [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation is conducted using objective ground-truth dataset categorical labels on held-out test splits without reliance on learned or automated surrogate judges.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Accuracy, macro-averaged precision, recall, and F1-score computed against ground-truth labels on the 30% test sets [E31e576869c0657c4-B0047, E31e576869c0657c4-B0050].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss with the Adam optimizer over 10 epochs on 70% training splits, selecting the checkpoint with the highest test accuracy [E31e576869c0657c4-B0046, E31e576869c0657c4-B0047].

primary.limitations: The authors transparently acknowledge that evaluation is limited to offline testing on small, controlled datasets without testing in-the-wild robustness or real end-to-end cloud latency and throughput [E31e576869c0657c4-B0006, E31e576869c0657c4-B0065].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology describes standard image preprocessing (grayscale conversion, resizing to 224x224, 3-channel replication) and fine-tuning an ImageNet-pretrained ViT-small model using Adam and cross-entropy loss [E31e576869c0657c4-B0029, E31e576869c0657c4-B0043, E31e576869c0657c4-B0046]. However, while the paper outlines a theoretical SqueezeViT architecture with local-global feature fusion, the text explicitly clarifies that the dedicated local-branch fusion module was not part of the trained and evaluated model pipeline [E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].
primary.quality_rationale: The contribution is modest, essentially consisting of fine-tuning an off-the-shelf ViT-small model on three legacy datasets. The gap between the formulated squeeze-fusion method and the actually evaluated architecture, combined with the lack of direct baseline comparisons and missing cloud/edge empirical runtime evaluations despite the paper's central title and theme, warrants an uncertain assessment.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript evaluates fine-tuning a compact ViT-small backbone for seven-class facial expression recognition across three benchmark datasets (CK+, JAFFE, and KDEF), motivated as a computationally efficient layer for cloud storage pipelines [E31e576869c0657c4-B0005, E31e576869c0657c4-B0011, E31e576869c0657c4-B0045].

multi-scale patch embedding stem and a depthwise-convolutional feed-forward network (DW-FFN) to
inject local inductive bias into the Transformer framework. Experimental results demonstrate that the
proposed architecture achieves an overall accuracy (OA) of 97.58% and a Kappa coefficient of 0.966
across 50,854 validation samples. Class-wise evaluation highlights exceptional performance in

challenging environment for evaluating model robustness against spatial decorrelation and atmospheric

significant Line-of-Sight (LOS) surface displacements across complex topographic terrain, presenting a
challenging environment for evaluating model robustness against spatial decorrelation and atmospheric
phase screens (Xie, 2025). The geographical context and the main fault systems of the study area are
illustrated in Fig. 1.

To create a supervised learning environment, the interferogram was labeled into discrete classes using a
combined approach of statistical estimation and expert validation.
Ground Truth Generation: Initially, the Maximum Likelihood Classification (MLC) algorithm was used to
categorize the phase values (Li et al., 2023). These results were then manually refined based on the
technical legends to ensure the accuracy of the training labels.
Displacement Scaling: The labeling process was governed by the physical parameters of the C-band SAR
signal. As shown in the technical legends (Fig. 3), the dataset is scaled to reflect a Line-of-Sight (LOS)
displacement range of approximately − 0.03 m (subsidence) to + 0.03 m (uplift). In the wrapped phase
domain, each full fringe cycle (-π to + π) corresponds to 2.8 cm of ground movement (Daramola et al.,
2025).

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No independent external physical measurements (e.g., GNSS, leveling, or independent geodetic models) are reported to corroborate the deformation classifications.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pixel classification metrics (OA, AA, Kappa, F1-score) computed against the same pseudo-ground truth labeling scheme on the single event.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss optimized against pseudo-ground truth pixel labels generated from Maximum Likelihood Classification and manual refinement.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims of robust deformation mapping and noise suppression across seismic events are evaluated on only one single interferogram event without independent geodetic validation (such as GNSS stations or independent seismic field data). Potential data leakage across spatial patches or adjacent pixels during pixel-level evaluation is unaddressed.
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation is conducted entirely on 50,854 validation pixels from a single earthquake interferogram whose pseudo-ground truth was generated by Maximum Likelihood Classification followed by manual refinement. Only a single standard ViT baseline is compared; established DInSAR unwrapping/deformation models or strong CNN benchmarks are omitted.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: No independent external physical measurements (such as continuous GNSS station displacements, leveling surveys, or external seismic fault models) are evaluated to corroborate the deformation classifications.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Pixel classification metrics (OA, AA, Kappa, F1-score) calculated against the same pseudo-ground truth labeling scheme on the single event.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Cross-entropy loss optimized against pseudo-ground truth pixel labels generated from Maximum Likelihood Classification and manual refinement.

primary.limitations: The study relies on a single seismic event and satellite acquisition pair. Ground truth relies partially on automated statistical classification (MLC) rather than independent in-situ physical measurements.
primary.method_assessment: The architecture combines multi-scale convolutional operations with standard self-attention mechanisms and depthwise-separable FFN blocks. However, the exact data splitting protocol (e.g., random pixel splitting vs. spatially disjoint split), dataset size details, training hyperparameters, and baseline implementation details are minimally described.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a sensible hybrid architecture concept, but the evaluation design carries substantial scientific uncertainty. Testing is limited to a single interferogram without clear spatial cross-validation controls, GNSS/ground-truth validation, or comparison against standard remote sensing deformation pipelines.
primary.scoped_contribution: The manuscript proposes INRA-Transformer, a hybrid Vision Transformer incorporating an Inception-based multi-scale patch embedding stem and a depthwise-convolutional feed-forward network to classify seismic surface deformation zones from Sentinel-1A DInSAR interferograms of the 6.1 Mw Sındırgı earthquake.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a sensible hybrid architecture concept, but the evaluation design carries substantial scientific uncertainty. Testing is limited to a single interferogram without clear spatial cross-validation controls, GNSS/ground-truth validation, or comparison against standard remote sensing deformation pipelines.

concerns: The primary result on the OAI test set is compared against prior studies that used different models, metrics, and evaluation conditions, making the claimed superiority not a controlled like-for-like comparison.

Headline performance values approach near-perfect levels while class-wise AP figures exceed pooled mAP by less than two points across classes with severe imbalance, raising unaddressed uncertainty about the reported detection and grading numbers.

The method is called Lorentzian distance but the formula presented is a sum of two log(1+x) terms, which is not the standard Lorentzian distance metric, leaving the mathematical foundation and stated properties unsupported.

Distance Intersection over Union (LD -IoU) localization loss integrated 
into the YOLOv8 framework. B y incorporating the Lorentzian distance into the conventional IoU formulation, the 
proposed loss provides a more robust representation of spatial discrepancy, enabling more accurate bounding -box 
regression. Experiments conducted on the OAI dataset demonstr ate that the proposed framework consistently 
outperforms the baseline YOLOv8 and existing IoU -based localization losses. The proposed LD -IoU-YOLOv8 
achieved 99.1% precision, 94.2% mAP@0.5:0.95, 99.6% mAP@0.5, and 98.8% recall, while reducing the Box Loss 
from 0.291 to 0.093, corresponding to an approximately 68% relative reduction. Furthermore, the proposed localization 
loss demonstrated faster convergence than the conventional IoU loss, achieving high mAP@0.5 in fewer training

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

blocking_reasons: The primary result on the OAI test set is compared against prior studies that used different models, metrics, and evaluation conditions, making the claimed superiority not a controlled like-for-like comparison.

Headline performance values approach near-perfect levels while class-wise AP figures exceed pooled mAP by less than two points across classes with severe imbalance, raising unaddressed uncertainty about the reported detection and grading numbers.

The method is called Lorentzian distance but the formula presented is a sum of two log(1+x) terms, which is not the standard Lorentzian distance metric, leaving the mathematical foundation and stated properties unsupported.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The manuscript reports external test-set evaluation and patient-level splitting measured with conventional ground-truth-derived metrics.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Precision, recall, mAP@0.5, and mAP@0.5:0.95 computed from manual ground-truth bounding boxes and KL labels on held-out and external test sets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised training with the proposed LD-IoU regression loss combined with classification loss under standard backpropagation.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported performance gains (e.g., 99.6% mAP@0.5, 94.2% mAP@0.5:0.95, and lower box loss on the OAI benchmark) are supported by direct head-to-head comparisons, ablation of normalization, and multi-seed confidence intervals [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0003, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0062, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0069, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0090].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical validation is comprehensive, comparing LD-IoU against eight alternative IoU loss functions under controlled settings, running ablation experiments, testing cross-architecture generalization across one-stage and two-stage detectors, reporting run-to-run variance across random seeds, performing external dataset testing, and checking patient-level data leakage [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0062, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0069, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0080, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0090, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0092, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0094].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The method was corroborated using standard external test sets (Digital Knee X-ray dataset) and held-out patient-level split evaluations on standard detection metrics [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0090, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0092, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0094].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard ground-truth benchmark metrics including mAP@0.5, mAP@0.5:0.95, Precision, and Recall computed on held-out test sets [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0038, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0044, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0087].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The proposed LD-IoU regression loss function combined with classification loss during supervised backpropagation training [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0033, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0047].

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly discuss constraints, including evaluation predominantly on X-ray radiography (leaving modalities like MRI and CT to future work), the need for larger external multi-cohort validation, and potential patient-level splitting shifts [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0099].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, mathematically defining the normalized Lorentzian distance normalized by the smallest enclosing bounding box and showing its direct plug-in integration into bounding box regression heads without extra learnable parameters [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0032, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0033].
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a clearly motivated, mathematically defined loss formulation supported by extensive, fair, and controlled comparative evaluations across loss baselines, detector families, and external test data with rigorous leakage and statistical checks [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0033, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0062, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0080, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0090, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0092, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0094].
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces Lorentzian Distance Intersection over Union (LD-IoU), a bounding-box regression loss integrating normalized Lorentzian center distance into standard IoU, and evaluates its performance for knee joint localization and Kellgren-Lawrence grading across YOLOv8 and multiple detector architectures on knee X-ray datasets [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0003, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0033, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0080].

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a clearly motivated, mathematically defined loss formulation supported by extensive, fair, and controlled comparative evaluations across loss baselines, detector families, and external test data with rigorous leakage and statistical checks [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0033, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0062, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0080, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0090, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0092, E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0094].
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors explicitly discuss constraints, including evaluation predominantly on X-ray radiography (leaving modalities like MRI and CT to future work), the need for larger external multi-cohort validation, and potential patient-level splitting shifts [E2c0b3fe0b7c7dfa4-B0099].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Independent cross-dataset and leave-one-attack-out evaluations on unseen manipulation types and benchmark datasets support the headline gains.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out test metrics including ACC, AUC, APCER, BPCER, ACER, HTER, FAR and FRR on official or subject-disjoint splits.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Binary cross-entropy loss against ground-truth real versus attack/spoof labels, trained end-to-end with Adam.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported gains over baseline architectures (CNN-based, ViT, and other hybrid models) are supported by empirical results across high- and low-quality video splits, cross-dataset transfers, and leave-one-attack-out settings.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The model is evaluated across multiple standard deepfake and face presentation attack benchmarks (FaceForensics++, Celeb-DF, DFDC, WildDeepfake, OULU-NPU, SiW, Replay-Attack) using cross-validation, official protocols, statistical significance testing (paired t-tests), and comprehensive ablation studies.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluations on independent cross-dataset benchmarks (Celeb-DF, DFDC, Wilde-DF, OULU-NPU Protocols 1-4) and cross-manipulation splits using objective error rates.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard classification performance metrics (ACC, AUC, ACER, APCER, BPCER, HTER) computed on held-out test splits and unseen benchmark datasets.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised binary cross-entropy loss against ground-truth bona fide versus attack/spoof labels using backpropagation with Adam.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently discuss remaining limitations, such as sensitivity to extreme compression and motion blur, the absence of confidence calibration analysis, and untested generalization to diffusion-based video generation models.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing OpenFace 2.0 FAU extraction, binary spatial mask projection, modulated self-attention formulas, adapted ResNet50 backbone layers, and sequence modeling with LSTM under binary cross-entropy optimization.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript presents a scoped architectural design with complete implementation configurations, rigorous comparative testing across multiple standard benchmark datasets, paired statistical tests, and explicit ablation verification.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper proposes a hybrid facial action unit (FAU)-guided vision transformer framework combining CNN local feature extraction, FAU-biased ViT self-attention, and an LSTM temporal aggregator for face presentation attack and deepfake detection.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript presents a scoped architectural design with complete implementation configurations, rigorous comparative testing across multiple standard benchmark datasets, paired statistical tests, and explicit ablation verification.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently discuss remaining limitations, such as sensitivity to extreme compression and motion blur, the absence of confidence calibration analysis, and untested generalization to diffusion-based video generation models.

Backend choice substantially reduces attacked
suppression latency, but no uncapped backend we
tested satisfies the declared suppression screen.
Following the deployment-realism concern of prior
work [ 15, 16], we replay identical attacked can-
didate arrays through three suppression imple-
mentations. Over the same 48 images the sup-
pression call's p95 is 635.35 ms on the deployed
NumPy path, 177.71 ms on torchvision CPU and
49.08 ms on torchvision CUDA. CPU arms use the
host clock. CUDA arms are bracketed by device
synchronization after a warm-up, since an unsyn-
chronized timing measures the kernel launch, not
the work. The host-to-device copy is excluded; at
0.183 ms p95 it changes neither ordering nor ver-
dict, so the CUDA figure understates a backend
fed from the host.
5

evidence.excerpt:
Top-K selection is a standard operation and we
claim no novelty for it. What is proposed here is its
use as a deployment-selected bound on attacker-
controlled work, with the value calibrated against
a declared deadline and its accuracy cost mea-
sured. Let C be the candidates surviving the
confidence threshold and N = |C|. Before NMS
we retain only CK = TopK( C, K), admitting for
N > K the K candidates smallest under the
lexicographic key ( −sj, j): argpartition on the
negated scores at index K − 1 locates the cutoff,
every candidate strictly above it is admitted, and
the remaining places go to candidates equal to it in
ascending index order. The tie rule is not a formal-
ity, NumPy's introselect being unstable and exact
ties reachable at fp16 or quantized scores. The cut
is O(N ) and adds no pairwise IoU comparison, the
term Eq. ( 4) bounds.
For a serial greedy NMS implementation,

evidence.excerpt:
Figure 3 evaluates several values of K under
three admission policies: the deployed global bud-
get, which admits at most K candidates in total,
and the per-class and per-level alternatives. Only
the global policy makes the admitted total a
declared quantity, so Eq. ( 4) applies to it alone.
The other two are plotted for completeness; equal
labels there are not equal admitted work, and the
curves are not a ranking. The operating point
K = 1024 reduces attacked suppression p95 to
4.28 ms. Its clean cost is the paired difference of
the last two rows of Table 1, 0.00064 AP@[ .50 :
.95], and 0.00060 when the clean evaluation is
replayed through the serving pool. Both are vali-
dation figures, while §3's headline accuracy is held
out, and a cost measured on one population can-
not be subtracted from an accuracy measured on
another; so we repeated the sweep on test-dev
with K fixed

served deadline
The cap reduces client-side p95 under attack by
a factor of 15.10, a median over five independent
A/B sessions, yet the defended requests still miss
De2e = 33 .3 ms every time. That is no contra-
diction: the work bound applies to suppression,
and TNMS ≤ Dsupp does not imply Le2e ≤ De2e.
Nor is the miss attributable to the attack alone.
Attacked images must be delivered losslessly, since
re-encoding at the quality this pool serves did
not preserve the perturbation, so comparing them
against the JPEG corpus varies two things at once.
We therefore re-encoded the same 48 sources into
the attacked arm's format and served all three
arms through the same pool at the same cap, in
ten sessions of 144 requests at ϵ = 2/255.
The adversary turns out not to be necessary for
the miss. Clean lossless images reach p95 66.20 ms
at a deadline-miss ratio of 0.927, against 61.20

The anchor grid sets the maximum candidate
count, so a cap validated on one output tensor
says little about another. We repeated the capture
and the sweep on the same detector family with-
out its P2 head: 33,600 anchors against 136,000,
a factor of four in the quantity that sets the
ceiling. K = 1024 holds the suppression budget
on both, 3.11 ms against 4.19 ms in the same
run, while the runtime's shipped ceiling of 30,000
misses on both, at 187.30 and 342.96 ms. This is
suppression replay only; no accuracy claim is made
for the second model, and the bound is estab-
lished for the two geometries tested rather than
for anchor-based detectors in general.

didate distribution is more than an order of mag-
nitude sparser than VisDrone's, while attacked
counts land at much the same level on both.
Their ratio therefore rises to 1777.19, which mea-

clean capped deadline-miss ratio is 0.0, so the

tract. Transfer across input distributions is what
EV ADE found published attacks to lack [ 15]; we
report it for the defense.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The final evaluation uses objective wall-clock latency, deadline-miss ratio, and held-out COCO AP metrics measured on the exported serving path, which are independent of the differentiable surrogate used to craft attacks.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Client-scope p95 latency, deadline-miss ratio, and COCO AP@[.50:.95] on held-out test data.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Projected gradient ascent on a differentiable surrogate maximizing the count of candidates passing the confidence threshold before NMS.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: All claims are strictly supported by paired measurements and realistic controls; the authors avoid overclaiming by explicitly showing that the hardened artifact still fails end-to-end deadline requirements due to payload decode overheads, thus proving bounded suppression is necessary but not sufficient.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical evaluation rigorously compares clean and attacked pipelines across datasets (VisDrone2019, BDD100K) and architectures, explicitly separating client, worker, and suppression timing scopes while reporting p95 tail latencies and deadline-miss ratios under thermal throttling and varied payload encodings.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final evaluation evaluates objective hardware execution times, deadline compliance across distinct backends, and standard mAP metrics on held-out test sets without any shared surrogate loss.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: System-level wall-clock 95th percentile latency, deadline-miss ratio (DMR), and COCO AP@[.50:.95] detection accuracy on held-out test data.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Projected gradient ascent maximizing the count of candidate bounding boxes passing the confidence threshold before NMS.

primary.limitations: The authors transparently report that the defense only bounds stage-specific algorithmic IoU comparisons without guaranteeing hardware worst-case execution time or preventing end-to-end violations caused by upstream bottlenecks like image decompression.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing a deterministic PGD-based candidate inflation attack, a lexicographic Top-K selection rule calibrated against a declared deadline, and stage-isolated latency profiling spanning multiple software backends (NumPy, PyTorch CPU/CUDA) and hardware platforms (RTX 4090 pool and Raspberry Pi 4B).
primary.quality_rationale: The work provides rigorous experimental design, meticulous profiling across independent scopes, transparent negative results regarding full serving pipeline compliance, and thorough ablation across models, datasets, and platforms.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper demonstrates that bounding candidate box admissions prior to non-maximum suppression (NMS) effectively limits attacker-controlled latency inflation in real-time object detection, while precisely quantifying the resulting held-out accuracy loss and showing that post-NMS bottleneck shifts (such as image decoding) prevent stage-level latency bounds from guaranteeing end-to-end deadline integrity.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work provides rigorous experimental design, meticulous profiling across independent scopes, transparent negative results regarding full serving pipeline compliance, and thorough ablation across models, datasets, and platforms.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors transparently report that the defense only bounds stage-specific algorithmic IoU comparisons without guaranteeing hardware worst-case execution time or preventing end-to-end violations caused by upstream bottlenecks like image decompression.

eval-
uated within a single architecture, leaving open whether their effective-
ness stems from the merging mechanism itself or from the specific de-
coder they are paired with. We extend Graph-Guided Token Merging
(G2TM), a single module inserted early in a ViT-based network, beyond
its original Segmenter setting. We evaluate G2TM across three semantic
segmentation frameworks (Segmenter, SETR, EoMT) and three decoder
families (Linear, Transformer-, convolution-based), as well as standard
ViT image classification. Our results show that G2TM's behavior and
accuracy–efficiency trade-off are consistent across every tested architec-
ture for a given backbone size, indicating that its effectiveness is a prop-
erty of the encoder rather than the decoder. G2TM also generalizes well
to image classification, achieving an even smaller degradation in accu-
racy compared to semantic segmentation.

To address token redundancy in ViTs, we propose Graph-Guided Token Merging
(G2TM), a token merging framework based on graph theory. As illustrated in
Figure 1, G2TM is inserted once in a chosen Transformer block of the encoder,
unlike prior token merging methods which typically reduce the token sequence
iteratively or across multiple layers. In practice, we favor insertion in shallow
stages, typically after the first or second attention layer, since reducing the token
sequence early maximizes computational savings in subsequent self-attention
operations.

To control the merging granularity, we define a thresholdτprior to training (see
Section 4) and apply it to the cosine similarity scores. Thereby, we remove all
edges whose weights are below this threshold, disconnecting tokens that are not
similar enough (see Figure 2.b). The number of removed edges depends on both
the input image and the chosen threshold value.
After the edge cut, the remaining structure of the graphGconsists of several
disconnected subgraphs, that are called connected components in graph theory.
In G2TM, each of them represents a group of locally similar tokens. We apply
a Breadth-First-Search (BFS) algorithm to the graphG, to retrieve the indices
of the tokens belonging to each connected component whose size is greater than
1 (i.e.: comprising more than 1 token). Thus, we obtain a set of tokens for

In terms of numbers, assuming a decrease in mIoU of at most2points on
ADE20K dataset, G2TM achieves a consistent drop in GFLOPs of up to47%
and throughput improves by up to74%, when the original model's throughput
is below approximately100FPS. Above this cutoff, G2TM's own overhead is no
longer offset by the subsequent attention savings, and throughput even decreases
despite a genuine reduction in GFLOPs. Together, these results position G2TM
as a decoder-agnostic and broadly transferable token merging strategy, whose
deployment should be guided by the pre-training recipe, the target task and
dataset, as well as the throughput of the original model it is applied to.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The optimization signal is supervised task loss with a fixed threshold curriculum, while the headline outcomes are measured with held-out validation ground-truth metrics (mIoU, Top-1) and hardware profiling (FPS, GFLOPs), which are independent of the training objective.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Held-out validation ground-truth metrics (mIoU on ADE20K/Cityscapes, Top-1 on ImageNet-1k) plus measured FPS and computed GFLOPs.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Supervised cross-entropy/segmentation loss with backpropagation and a fixed threshold curriculum for G2TM edge pruning.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported experimental data support the claims: token counts and accuracy retention remain consistent across varied decoder heads for a given backbone, while throughput and FLOPs improve consistently on compute-heavy models, and pre-training distributions directly explain performance differences.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The empirical study comprehensively tests three semantic segmentation frameworks (Segmenter, SETR, EoMT) across four backbone scales on ADE20K and Cityscapes, as well as image classification on ImageNet-1k, measuring standard validation metrics (mIoU, Top-1 accuracy, GFLOPs, and GPU throughput). Extensive ablations examine Proportional Attention, off-the-shelf application, pre-training objectives (AugReg vs DINOv2), and input resolution.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Final model evaluations rely strictly on held-out standard benchmark ground-truth labels and external hardware compute metrics, entirely independent of the optimization process.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Standard validation ground-truth metrics (mean IoU on ADE20K/Cityscapes validation sets and Top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1k) along with hardware profiling (measured FPS and FLOPs).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Standard supervised cross-entropy and segmentation task loss optimization using backpropagation, with a fixed threshold curriculum for edge pruning.

primary.limitations: The authors explicitly note and analyze limitations, including reduced throughput on lightweight models (baseline throughput over 100 FPS) where module overhead exceeds attention savings, degradation under uncurated off-the-shelf deployment on small models, and failure on representations with oversmoothed cosine similarity profiles (such as DINOv2 without adjustment).
primary.method_assessment: G2TM constructs an undirected 4-neighborhood graph of patch tokens in an early transformer block, prunes edges below a cosine similarity threshold, fuses connected components via average pooling, and unmerges before decoder operations. The training adaptation via threshold curricula and masked attention is clearly formulated.
primary.quality_rationale: The manuscript delivers a rigorous, well-controlled systematic study of an efficiency module across diverse architectures and tasks. The experimental design is thorough, negative/boundary conditions are transparently discussed and analyzed, and claims match the evidence.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper presents a systematic empirical evaluation of Graph-Guided Token Merging (G2TM) across multiple vision transformer backbones, tasks, and decoder architectures (linear, convolutional, and transformer-based), demonstrating that G2TM's token reduction behavior and accuracy-efficiency trade-offs are decoder-agnostic and primarily governed by backbone pre-training and target datasets.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The manuscript delivers a rigorous, well-controlled systematic study of an efficiency module across diverse architectures and tasks. The experimental design is thorough, negative/boundary conditions are transparently discussed and analyzed, and claims match the evidence.

concerns: The paper presents a comparative study but does not establish its claimed contribution of a first comprehensive comparison: the literature review itself lists ViT and fusion models already applied and evaluated, the models compared are standard baselines rather than new methods, and no independent test-set verification of the headline results is supplied. Multiple stated performance values for nearly identical measures are inconsistent, such as the conclusion reporting TransUNet mIoU 0.64 and Dice 0.54 while Table IV reports 0.67 and 0.52, so the reported claims cannot be treated as scientifically reliable.

The central fairness claim is not supported by the noted optimization signals in Table III: U-Net and TransUNet use Dice loss while ViT uses Cross-Entropy, and batch sizes, maximum epochs, and early-stopping dynamics differ, so the alleged rigorous gold-standard comparison does not establish equivalence of training conditions. Such protocol mismatch can materially distort Dice and mIoU rankings and invalidates the central conclusion of this comparative benchmark.

The headline results are reported from validation curves and best-epoch selection rather than a held-out test assessment. The stated best-performing model was selected using peak validation mIoU, yet no test-split metrics are actually reported, even though the paper earlier declares a test split, meaning the results may have been selected for the very metric being reported.
scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The study offers an empirical benchmarking exercise, but methodological inconsistencies in training setups (differing loss functions, epochs, and batch sizes) prevent a rigorous apples-to-apples architectural comparison. Combined with reporting peak validation scores rather than transparent test split results, scientific certainty is insufficient for promotion.
